In this paper, we address this problem by introducing and studying , which measure the rate at which perturbations of initial conditions grow or decay when viewed through a chosen observable, rather than in the full phase space. For globally coupled maps, we consider finite-time observable Lyapunov exponents and define their mean-field counterpart by first taking the infinite-system limit and then the long-time limit. Our main result shows that, for a broad class of symmetric macroscopic observables, these exponents turn out to be determined by the linearisation of the self-consistent transfer operator, which is the nonlinear operator governing the evolution of the population distribution. We then apply this result to weakly coupled uniformly expanding maps and prove that their mean-field Lyapunov exponents are negative near a stationary mean-field state. Thus, although the microscopic dynamics is chaotic, perturbations decay at the macroscopic level. Our results provide a rigorous framework for distinguishing microscopic from macroscopic chaos in large interacting systems.
tldr: The paper introduces observable Lyapunov exponents to rigorously distinguish microscopic chaos from macroscopic stability in globally coupled maps in the mean-field limit.
motivation: Large coupled systems can be chaotic at the microscopic level yet exhibit stable collective macroscopic behaviour, and distinguishing these two forms of instability has been an open problem in the physics literature.
method: The authors define finite-time observable Lyapunov exponents and their mean-field counterparts by taking the infinite-system limit followed by the long-time limit, and relate them to the linearisation of the self-consistent transfer operator governing the population distribution.
result: For a broad class of symmetric macroscopic observables the mean-field exponents are determined by the linearised self-consistent transfer operator; for weakly coupled uniformly expanding maps they prove these exponents are negative near a stationary mean-field state, so macroscopic perturbations decay despite microscopic chaos.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for distinguishing microscopic from macroscopic chaos in large interacting systems, using observable-based Lyapunov exponents rather than full phase-space instabilities.

title: The Risk-Sensitive Schr\"odinger Bridge: Is Not A Kl Projection
authors: Hamidreza Behjoo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Schr\"odinger bridge owes its computational power to a single structural fact: by Girsanov's theorem the controlled problem is a Kullback--Leibler (KL) projection onto a fixed reference measure, solvable by alternating projections. This letter shows that the fact does not survive risk sensitivity. When the expected path cost is replaced by the entropic risk measure and both endpoint marginals are kept as hard constraints, the resulting fixed-point bridge value [MATH] (the soft-problem value at the multiplier that enforces the terminal constraint) admits no representation as a constrained KL minimum against any fixed path-space reference with a regular endpoint law (a class strictly larger than the uniformly elliptic diffusion references: no Markov property is required), even allowing an additive normalisation depending on the initial marginal. Moreover, no single reference generates the one-parameter family in the risk parameter. The obstruction is computed in closed form: the Gaussian bridge value violates, by exactly [MATH], a heat equation that any Gaussian smoothing of a fixed endpoint density must obey. In place of the projection, the theory rests on a terminal-multiplier fixed point and an asymmetric factorisation penalising the score energy of the backward factor.
tldr: This paper proves that the risk-sensitive Schrödinger bridge cannot be represented as a Kullback-Leibler projection onto a fixed reference measure, unlike the classical risk-neutral case.
motivation: The Schrödinger bridge problem's computational tractability relies on its formulation as a KL projection, but it is unclear whether this structure survives when expected cost is replaced by a risk measure.
method: The author analyzes the entropic risk measure version of the Schrödinger bridge with hard endpoint marginal constraints and shows, via a closed-form Gaussian computation, that no fixed reference measure with regular endpoint law can generate the bridge value as a constrained KL minimum.
result: The Gaussian bridge value violates a heat equation that any fixed endpoint density must satisfy, by an explicit amount, and no single reference generates the one-parameter family in the risk parameter.
conclusion: Risk-sensitive Schrödinger bridges rest on a terminal-multiplier fixed point and an asymmetric factorization penalizing backward score energy, rather than a KL projection.

title: Boundary Singular Scattering Enables Coherent Perfect Absorption And Lasing Without Resonators
authors: Letian Yu, Xu Zheng, Cesare Soci, Y. D. Chong, Baile Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scattering singularities are features conventionally associated with resonant scattering bodies, which correspond to the zeros and poles of a scattering matrix, and manifest as coherent perfect absorption and lasing respectively. Here, we show that they can emerge solely from an interface, eliminating the need for any resonant body. We introduce boundary singular scattering, whereby an interface between two non-Hermitian media supports coherent perfect absorption, lasing, or both. Despite these singular responses, the two adjoining media are in parity-time (PT)-unbroken phases, with entirely real bulk spectra. This phenomenon originates from a singular boundary mode-matching condition unique to non-Hermitian systems, not from any underlying resonant modes. We demonstrate it experimentally in a programmable synthetic photonic lattice, and show coherent switching between perfect absorption and lasing by controlling only the relative phase of the incident beams. The same mechanism further generalizes from mirror-symmetric interfaces to asymmetric interfaces with dissimilar bulk dispersions. Our work establishes boundaries as a previously unexplored origin of scattering singularities, opening a resonator-free route to coherent perfect absorption, lasing, and other singular wave phenomena.
tldr: The paper shows that scattering singularities producing coherent perfect absorption and lasing can arise purely from an interface between two PT-unbroken non-Hermitian media, with no resonant body needed.
motivation: Coherent perfect absorption and lasing are conventionally tied to resonant scattering bodies whose scattering matrices have zeros and poles; the authors ask whether such singularities can instead originate from a boundary alone.
method: They derive a singular boundary mode-matching condition for non-Hermitian interfaces and verify the predicted phenomena in a programmable synthetic photonic lattice, also generalizing to asymmetric interfaces with dissimilar bulk dispersions.
result: Interfaces between PT-unbroken media with entirely real bulk spectra support coherent perfect absorption, lasing, or both, switchable via the relative phase of incident beams.
conclusion: Boundaries constitute a previously unexplored origin of scattering singularities, enabling resonator-free coherent perfect absorption and lasing.

title: Anti-Localization Uplink Communications In Satellite-Terrestrial Systems
authors: Ranran Sun, Bin Yang, Yulong Shen, Yuanyu Zhang, Xiaohong Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the anti-localization uplink communication in a satellite-terrestrial system, where a ground transmitter Alice communicates with a legitimate satellite receiver Bob in the presence of multiple cooperative adversarial satellites attempting to localize Alice with the time difference of arrival (TDOA) technique. Specifically, we propose a cooperative jamming-based scheme for such anti-localization communication,in which Alice exploits the superposition coding with power allocation to simultaneously transmit information/jamming signals for communication with Bob and for confusing signal detection/TDOA measurement at adversarial satellites, while Bob employs the combining vector technique to enhance the desired information signal and also suppress the jamming. We define a localization error probability (LEP) metric to jointly depict both the impacts of signal detection and TDOA measurement on localization performance, and then develop a theoretical framework for the LEP modeling under the proposed scheme. We further explore the joint optimal design of jamming coding and power for LEP maximization, subject to the constraints of AliceBob communication reliability and Alice's transmit power. An effective sample average approximation method is also provided to tackle this non-convex optimization problem. Finally, extensive numerical results are illustrated to validate our theoretical models and demonstrate how the cooperative jamming helps to provide an anti-localization guarantee while ensuring communication reliability.
tldr: This paper proposes a cooperative jamming and superposition-coding scheme to prevent adversarial satellites from localizing a terrestrial transmitter via TDOA while maintaining reliable uplink communication.
motivation: Ground transmitters in satellite-terrestrial systems are vulnerable to localization by adversarial satellites using time-difference-of-arrival measurements, which can compromise user privacy and security.
method: Alice uses superposition coding with power allocation to transmit information and jamming signals simultaneously, while Bob applies combining-vector techniques; a localization error probability (LEP) metric is defined and a sample average approximation solves the joint jamming-coding and power optimization.
result: Theoretical LEP modeling and numerical results validate that cooperative jamming provides anti-localization guarantees while satisfying Alice-Bob communication reliability and transmit power constraints.
conclusion: Cooperative jamming with optimized coding and power allocation effectively balances anti-localization protection and communication reliability in satellite-terrestrial uplink systems.

title: Credible AUctions Via Mpc Gadgets: Bounding Information Leakage Under Abort
authors: Matheus Venturyne Xavier Ferreira
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The design of credible auctions---mechanisms where a revenue-maximizing auctioneer has no incentive to deviate from the protocol---faces a fundamental cryptographic barrier when the auctioneer controls shill bidders. While a natural approach is to use Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) to remove the trusted auctioneer, the impossibility of fair coin flipping of Cleve (1986) implies that monolithic MPC protocols grant the auctioneer a "free option": they can learn the auction's outcome and unilaterally abort if the revenue is unsatisfactory. Cryptographic commitments with ex-ante penalties mitigate this abort asymmetry, but no finite penalty suffices for heavy-tailed distributions. We circumvent this barrier by introducing the MPC Decomposition Principle. Rather than encrypting the entire mechanism, we use MPC strictly as an information-restriction tool. We isolate the winner determination problem into a minimal MPC gadget that computes and reveals the winner's identity but no payment information. This qualitative restriction mathematically bounds the information leaked upon an abort. By combining this gadget with sequential revelation and finite economic penalties, we design the Sequential Revelation Auction (SRA). We prove that bounding the information leakage strictly bounds the value of the free option, showing that a penalty of [MATH] is sufficient for credibility, and tight: for equal-revenue distributions, every smaller penalty admits a profitable deviation. Using constant-round MPC, the SRA resolves an open question of Akbarpour and Li (2020) and Ferreira and Weinberg (2020) by providing a constant-round, incentive-compatible, revenue-optimal credible auction for all product distributions with vanishing revenue tails.
tldr: The paper introduces an MPC decomposition principle to design credible auctions that bound information leakage under abort using minimal MPC gadgets and finite penalties.
motivation: Credible auction design faces a cryptographic barrier: monolithic MPC protocols let a revenue-maximizing auctioneer learn the outcome and abort if revenue is unsatisfactory, and no finite penalty works for heavy-tailed distributions.
method: The author isolates winner determination into a minimal MPC gadget that reveals only the winner's identity and no payment information, then combines it with sequential revelation and economic penalties to construct the Sequential Revelation Auction (SRA).
result: A finite penalty is proven sufficient for credibility and tight for equal-revenue distributions, and constant-round MPC yields an incentive-compatible, revenue-optimal credible auction for all product distributions with vanishing revenue tails.
conclusion: Bounding information leakage via MPC gadgets strictly bounds the value of the abort option, resolving an open question of Akbarpour and Li (2020) and Ferreira and Weinberg (2020).

title: Analytical Solution Of The Nonlinear Boltzmann Equation For Multicomponent Systems
authors: Linyuan Wei, Yi Wang, Jin Hu, Baoyi Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present exact analytical solutions to the nonlinear relativistic Boltzmann equation for homogeneous, isotropic massless multi-component systems with non-isotropic scattering cross sections. For a two-component system, we identify three distinct classes of exact solutions, each corresponding to specific constraints among initial energy densities, particle number densities, and scattering cross sections. These solutions comprise the equilibrium state and two novel classes: a hybrid structure featuring a non-equilibrium Maxwell-Juttner distribution coupled with a nontrivial distribution; the former is unprecedented in kinetic theory, while the latter refers to nontrivial dynamics shared by both species, which is novel in the relativistic context.
tldr: Exact analytical solutions are derived for the nonlinear relativistic Boltzmann equation in homogeneous, isotropic massless multi-component systems.
motivation: The paper aims to understand non-equilibrium dynamics and find exact solutions in relativistic kinetic theory for multi-component systems.
method: The authors analytically solve the nonlinear relativistic Boltzmann equation for massless multi-component systems with non-isotropic scattering cross sections, identifying solution classes for a two-component system.
result: Three distinct classes of exact solutions are found for the two-component case: the equilibrium state and two novel non-equilibrium classes, including a hybrid Maxwell-Jüttner distribution coupled with a nontrivial distribution.
conclusion: The work advances relativistic kinetic theory by providing unprecedented exact solutions, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Temporal Interfaces In Metamaterials With Shape-Varying Inclusions
authors: Ishtiaque Rahman, Mohamed Hesham Mostafa, Viktar Asadchy
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temporal modulation of metamaterials is commonly achieved by varying constituent material properties, while changes in meta-atom geometry offer an additional means of controlling their effective response. Here, we develop an analytical and numerical framework for temporal scattering in metamaterials composed of cylindrical inclusions undergoing abrupt geometric transformations. Changing the radius of circular cylinders modifies the filling fraction and scalar in-plane effective permittivity, enabling temporal reflection, field amplification or attenuation, and frequency conversion. An area-preserving transformation from circular to elliptical cross sections introduces anisotropy, producing angle-dependent temporal scattering and redirecting the energy flow while conserving the wavevector. We derive these effects using effective-medium theory and temporal boundary conditions and compare the predictions with full-wave time-domain simulations. The simulations reproduce the main scattering and temporal-aiming trends, with larger angular deflections than predicted by the quasistatic model at higher permittivity contrasts. This suggests that moving toward the resonant regime may offer opportunities for stronger temporal aiming. These results identify inclusion geometry as a means of controlling wave amplitude, frequency, and energy-flow direction at temporal interfaces.
tldr: This paper develops analytical and numerical methods for temporal scattering in metamaterials whose cylindrical inclusions undergo abrupt geometric changes, enabling control over wave amplitude, frequency, and energy-flow direction.
motivation: Temporal modulation of metamaterials is typically achieved by changing material properties; this work explores how changing meta-atom geometry provides an additional route to control effective response.
method: The authors use effective-medium theory and temporal boundary conditions to derive scattering effects for circular and elliptical inclusions, and compare predictions with full-wave time-domain simulations.
result: Changing cylinder radius modifies filling fraction and permittivity, producing temporal reflection, field amplification/attenuation, and frequency conversion; an area-preserving circular-to-elliptical transformation induces anisotropy and angle-dependent temporal scattering, redirecting energy flow while conserving wavevector.
conclusion: Inclusion geometry offers a means to control wave amplitude, frequency, and energy-flow direction at temporal interfaces, with stronger effects expected in the resonant regime beyond the quasistatic model.

title: Free Semigroup Non-relativistic Phase Space States Quantisation
authors: Georgii Koniukov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantisation is considered as an action of classical point operators on field states at the Planck scale of the phase space. Emphasis is placed on the sequence of physical variables. A "state language/Dirac notation" for classical mechanics is introduced; in many cases, it replaces the principle of stationary action for conservative systems. Observed classical and quantum dynamics are considered as different vectorisations of the free semigroup contribution of time. There is a dream of describing classical dynamics as complex transformations of state vectors over such a free semigroup, rather than solving differential equations. The transition from the alphabet to states, from states to state functions, and from state functions to measurable quantities is managed by projectors. An attempt is made to provide a derivation of the Legendre transformation. The trivial multiplication of the potential energy by the wave function in the coordinate representation and its non-trivial operator action in the momentum representation are obtained without a Fourier transform nor the Planck scale. The quantisation procedure is divided into two stages: first, the action of point-like classical operators on field functions; and second, accounting for the physically finite scale of the Planck length against the backdrop of the possible infinitesimality in the classical phase space. The concept of an angle between states is introduced, defining the measure of "quantumness". The free semigroup time contribution is studied in the context of the Born rule.
tldr: The paper proposes a free-semigroup-based reformulation of non-relativistic phase-space quantization using classical state vectors and projectors, with applications to the Born rule and Legendre transformation.
motivation: The author aims to replace differential-equation approaches to classical and quantum dynamics with an algebraic state-vector language based on a free semigroup of time, possibly simplifying quantization and connecting classical and quantum descriptions.
method: The work introduces a Dirac-like notation for classical mechanics, treats quantization as point-like classical operators acting on field states at the Planck scale, and uses projectors to move between alphabets, states, state functions, and observables.
result: The formalism recovers the trivial multiplication of potential energy by the wave function in coordinate space and its nontrivial operator action in momentum space without Fourier transforms, and defines an angle between states as a measure of 'quantumness'.
conclusion: While the paper explores a mathematically speculative unification of classical and quantum dynamics via semigroup structures, it does not address the information-theoretic, thermodynamic, network, or hybrid-platform topics prioritized in the researcher's interests.

title: Floquet-Bloch Theory For Dispersive Time-varying Metasurfaces
authors: Mohammad Mojtaba Sadafi, Sandeep Inampudi, Hossein Mosallaei
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Light-matter interaction in time-varying metasurfaces brings about phenomena that transcend the limits of static systems. Temporal modulation enables energy exchange between light and matter, and electromagnetic fields are coupled in both momentum and frequency, with implications across a broad range of photonic applications. Nevertheless, a precise description of such systems necessitates a theory that captures the intertwined effects of spatiotemporal variations while accounting for dispersion in a causal manner, as realistic optical materials exhibit frequency-dependent response and finite temporal memory. Here, a self-contained Floquet-Bloch theory is developed to capture the response of dispersive, time-varying metasurfaces, respecting causality through physically consistent constitutive relations. The theory treats spatial periodicity, nonadiabatic temporal modulation, and material dispersion within a unified formalism, providing access not only to the metasurface's scattering response but also to its inherent modal structure. The formulation is validated against full-wave simulations. As illustrative examples, it is first applied to asymmetric Floquet harmonic generation in an excitonic time-varying metasurface, where excitonic dispersion enables selective harmonic enhancement. It is then used to investigate metasurface-based photonic time crystals, revealing how modal dispersion governs momentum-bandgap formation and dynamics. This work establishes a comprehensive platform for understanding dispersive, time-varying metasurfaces and their underlying physical mechanisms.
tldr: The paper develops a Floquet-Bloch formalism for dispersive, time-varying metasurfaces, capturing causal material dispersion, spatial periodicity, and nonadiabatic temporal modulation within a unified scattering and modal framework.
motivation: Time-varying metasurfaces enable light-matter energy exchange and momentum-frequency coupling, but existing theories neglect causal dispersion and finite temporal memory of realistic optical materials.
method: A self-contained Floquet-Bloch theory is constructed with physically consistent constitutive relations enforcing causality, validated against full-wave simulations and applied to excitonic harmonic generation and photonic time crystals.
result: The theory reveals selective harmonic enhancement from excitonic dispersion and shows how modal dispersion governs momentum-bandgap formation and dynamics in metasurface-based photonic time crystals.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive platform for understanding dispersive, time-varying metasurfaces, but remains a classical electromagnetic/photonic theory with no quantum information or thermodynamics content.

title: Calibrating Sensing Drift In Tomographic Inversion
authors: Xiang Huang, Parth Brahmbhatt, Chang Meng, Zichao Wendy Di
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scanning-probe x-ray tomography is useful for imaging nanoscale structures of a sample. The image resolution, which can reach down to 10 nm by the increased brightness and coherence of the x-ray optics, however, is highly susceptible to experimental error. Failure to address these errors can lead to a smeared image and, in the worst case, to misinterpretation of the imaged object's structure. In this work, we present a novel optimization-based approach to calibrate a common yet challenging source of experimental error, the drifts of the scanning positions, while simultaneously reconstructing the object. This approach uses the coupled and complementary information from different measurements to enforce consistency between the measurements and the reconstruction. We illustrate the proposed approach on both synthetic and real tomography images and show its superior performance compared with reconstruction without explicit error calibration.
tldr: The paper proposes an optimization-based method to jointly calibrate scanning-position drift and reconstruct the object in scanning-probe x-ray tomography.
motivation: Nanoscale x-ray tomography resolution is severely degraded by experimental errors such as drift of scanning positions, which cause image smearing and potential misinterpretation of sample structure.
method: The authors formulate a joint optimization that couples information from multiple complementary measurements to enforce consistency between the measured data and the reconstructed object, simultaneously estimating drift and recovering the image.
result: Demonstrations on both synthetic and real tomography data show superior reconstruction quality compared with reconstruction performed without explicit drift calibration.
conclusion: Explicit optimization-based drift calibration materially improves scanning-probe x-ray tomography, mitigating a common and challenging source of experimental error.

title: Grothendieck Rings Of Module Categories Over Drinfeld Doubles
authors: Dmitri Nikshych
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and [MATH] a finite group. We realize the based Grothendieck ring [MATH] of [MATH]-module categories as the degree-two cocycle-decorated double Burnside ring and derive an explicit Clifford formula for multiplication and for the action of [MATH] on the Grothendieck group of [MATH]-module categories. We determine the extremal based ideals, study factorization through smaller groups, and prove a Mackey theorem for standard two-sided subgroup inductions. We prove that [MATH] is semisimple exactly when [MATH] is cyclic. We study the Brauer--Picard action on indecomposable [MATH]-module categories and show that it is transitive exactly when [MATH] is abelian of square-free exponent. For abelian [MATH], we determine the possible abstract group types of Lagrangian subgroups of [MATH], apply the known orthogonal classification in the homocyclic case, and exhibit same-type nonconjugate Lagrangians for mixed exponents.
tldr: A pure algebra paper realizing Grothendieck rings of module categories over Drinfeld doubles as cocycle-decorated double Burnside rings and studying their algebraic properties.
motivation: To understand the algebraic structure of Grothendieck rings of module categories over Drinfeld doubles and their applications to factorization, Brauer-Picard actions, and Lagrangian subgroups.
method: Uses a realization as degree-two cocycle-decorated double Burnside rings, derives a Clifford formula for multiplication and group action, and analyzes extremal ideals, Mackey theorem, semisimplicity, and Brauer-Picard transitivity via group theory.
result: Proves semisimplicity exactly when the group is cyclic; Brauer-Picard action is transitive exactly when the group is abelian of square-free exponent; determines possible Lagrangian subgroup types and exhibits nonconjugate same-type Lagrangians for mixed exponents.
conclusion: Characterizes algebraic properties of these Grothendieck rings, contributing to pure representation theory and category theory, but not directly aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Critical Surface For Two Component Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Wenshuai Peng, Xiaoyu Zeng, Qidi Zhang, Huan-Song Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the existence of ground states for two-component Bose--Einstein condensates with intraspecies interactions [MATH] and interspecies interaction [MATH]. By carefully investigating an associated auxiliary minimization problem, we prove the existence of a unique, continuous, critical surface [MATH] between [MATH] and [MATH]. This surface provides a complete classification for the existence of minimizers: ground states exist for [MATH] and do not exist for [MATH]. Additionally, when the trapping potentials are continuous at a common zero point, there is no ground state for [MATH]. Our results close the gap case [MATH] when [MATH] in literature, significantly extending the results in .
tldr: A rigorous mathematical analysis proving the existence of a unique continuous critical surface separating regimes with and without ground states in two-component Bose-Einstein condensates.
motivation: Two-component BECs exhibit rich phase behavior driven by the competition between intraspecies and interspecies interactions, but a complete classification of when ground states exist was not established, leaving a gap in the case of equal/critical interaction strengths.
method: The authors formulate an auxiliary minimization problem and analyze it rigorously using variational and functional-analytic techniques to characterize the threshold surface in the intra-/interspecies interaction parameter plane, including the case of trapping potentials with a common zero.
result: They establish a unique continuous critical surface dividing the parameter space into regions where minimizers (ground states) exist and where they do not, and show that no ground state exists when trapping potentials are continuous at a common zero point, thereby closing a previously open gap case.
conclusion: The work provides a complete existence classification for two-component BEC ground states, significantly extending prior results, though it remains a pure nonlinear PDE/variational analysis with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum networking.

title: Only Pay What You Must Spend: On-Demand Privacy Budget Payment For Differentially Private Rag
authors: Zhonghao Sun, Zhiliang Tian, Xinyue Fang, Shuo Ma, Juhua Zhang, Yiping Song, Dongsheng Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying large language models (LLMs) on sensitive data via Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) introduces severe privacy risks. Recent studies apply Differential Privacy (DP) to LLMs with RAG for formal privacy guarantees. However, existing DP-RAG frameworks rapidly exhaust the privacy budget. Although recent efforts attempt to save the budget by narrowing the retrieval scope or sparsifying private generation, these methods themselves cumulatively consume the budget, whereas they could actually rely merely on public information or at a negligible one-time privacy cost. This mismatch fails to align budget expenditure with the model's actual reliance on private data, causing substantial waste on operations that require no private access. To address this, we propose SparsePay-RAG, adopting "only pay what you must spend" as its core principle. Using public information as a zero-privacy prior, it charges the privacy budget only for the private increment. Specifically, SparsePay-RAG narrows the retrieval scope via public topic-guided clustering, adaptively controls private access frequency without privacy cost through isotonic cross-layer trajectory fitting, and compresses per-access budget via DP contrastive decoding. Under strong privacy constraints, experiments show SparsePay-RAG achieves superior privacy-utility trade-offs over baselines.
tldr: SparsePay-RAG is a differentially private retrieval-augmented generation framework that charges privacy budget only for the private information increment, using public information as a zero-privacy prior.
motivation: Applying differential privacy to LLM-based RAG systems rapidly exhausts the privacy budget because existing methods waste budget on operations that rely only on public information.
method: The framework narrows retrieval scope via public topic-guided clustering, adaptively controls private access frequency through isotonic cross-layer trajectory fitting, and compresses per-access budget using DP contrastive decoding.
result: Under strong privacy constraints, SparsePay-RAG achieves superior privacy-utility trade-offs compared to baseline DP-RAG methods.
conclusion: Aligning privacy budget expenditure with actual reliance on private data enables more efficient and practical differentially private retrieval-augmented generation.

title: DNNsolver: Accurate And Efficient Deep Learning Modeling Of Polarization-Sensitive Diffractive Neural Networks
authors: Shuyi Wang, Hong-Bo Sun, Linhan Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffractive neural networks (DNNs), composed of cascaded diffractive layers, offer a promising platform for high-speed optical computing. However, accurate and efficient modeling of high-density, polarization-sensitive DNNs remains challenging. Conventional model based on thin element approximation (TEA) fails to capture electromagnetic coupling within layers, while full-wave simulations such as finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods are computationally expensive. Here, we propose DNNsolver, a deep learning-based electromagnetic surrogate model that learns the scattering response of diffractive layers. By predicting the scattering matrix rather than source-dependent output fields, DNNsolver decouples the incident wavefront from the model and could be applied to arbitrary input fields. A local scattering kernel and sliding-window strategy further allow efficient modeling of DNNs with arbitrary spatial sizes. For single diffractive layer under random speckle illumination, DNNsolver achieves an average mean squared error (MSE) of 0.0095 and about 10^6-fold speedup compared with FDTD simulations. DNNsolver is further applied to the optimization of a trilayer polarization-multiplexed image classifier, which exhibits better agreement with FDTD simulations than its TEA-based counterpart. Our work provides an accurate and efficient framework for the design and optimization of high-density, polarization-sensitive DNNs.
tldr: DNNsolver is a deep-learning surrogate model that predicts the scattering matrix of diffractive neural network layers, enabling accurate and ~10^6-fold faster modeling than FDTD for polarization-sensitive diffractive optical computing.
motivation: Accurate modeling of high-density, polarization-sensitive diffractive neural networks is difficult because thin-element approximation ignores inter-layer electromagnetic coupling while full-wave FDTD simulation is prohibitively expensive.
method: A deep-learning surrogate learns each diffractive layer's scattering matrix (decoupling it from the incident field), combined with a local scattering kernel and sliding-window strategy to scale to arbitrary spatial sizes.
result: DNNsolver achieves MSE ~0.0095 under random speckle illumination with ~10^6-fold speedup over FDTD, and yields a trilayer polarization-multiplexed image classifier that agrees better with FDTD than its TEA-based counterpart.
conclusion: The framework offers an accurate and efficient tool for designing and optimizing high-density, polarization-sensitive diffractive neural networks for high-speed optical computing.

title: The Next Fourier Transform: Rewiring, Representation, And Artificial Mathematical Creativity
authors: Luca Fanelli
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What distinguishes the solution of a difficult mathematical problem from a conceptual revolution? Some mathematical innovations do more than establish new results: they reorganize the relations among problems. We propose to describe such events through changes in the transfer structure of mathematics, namely the pattern determining which problems can naturally inform one another, which methods can move between them, and which new questions become accessible. The eighteenth-century controversy over the vibrating string provides our central historical case. D'Alembert found a famous model for wave propagation, Bernoulli proposed a modal interpretation, Euler broadened the class of admissible profiles, and Lagrange constructed a finite-dimensional strategy based on modal decomposition. Later, Fourier analysis gave the trigonometric language in which all the previous descriptions can interact. This motivates our Rewiring Thesis: a conceptual revolution is a persistent, large-scale reorganization of transfer relations among mathematical problems. The productive representation is one mechanism capable of producing such rewiring, but some stress tests (involving Galois, Riemann, Lebesgue-Schwartz and Wiles) show that it is not the only one. The musical notation provides an independent case in which the representation becomes operationally generative without being informationally complete. The resulting framework suggests a stronger criterion for artificial mathematical creativity than problem solving alone. The relevant question is not merely "whether AI can solve a famous conjecture", but "whether it can recognize that an inherited conceptual organization is itself an obstruction and produce a new one that reorganizes several problems at once". In this sense, the decisive achievement may be the invention of "the next Fourier transform".
tldr: The paper proposes a 'Rewiring Thesis' characterizing conceptual revolutions in mathematics as persistent reorganizations of transfer relations among problems, illustrated by the vibrating string controversy, and uses this to argue for a stronger criterion of artificial mathematical creativity.
motivation: The author wants to distinguish mere problem-solving from genuine conceptual innovation, and to articulate what it would mean for an AI to achieve the latter.
method: Historical case studies (d'Alembert, Bernoulli, Euler, Lagrange, Fourier) plus stress tests involving Galois, Riemann, Lebesgue-Schwartz, and Wiles, alongside musical notation as an independent case of operationally generative representation.
result: Conceptual revolutions are framed as large-scale rewiring of inter-problem transfer structures; productive representation is one mechanism for this rewiring but not the only one.
conclusion: A stronger criterion for artificial mathematical creativity is proposed: the decisive achievement would be inventing 'the next Fourier transform' by recognizing inherited conceptual organization as an obstruction and producing a reorganizing framework.

title: Adjoints, Order And Spectral Moduli On $l^2(t)$
authors: Mohamed Amine Ben Amor
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study adjoints of [MATH]-linear, [MATH]-strongly bounded operators on the conditional space [MATH] and the interaction between its Hilbert-type geometry and its Riesz-space order. This produces two natural operator moduli: the Riesz--Kantorovich order modulus and the spectral modulus [MATH]. After isolating the [MATH]-regular operators, we show that they form a Dedekind-complete order ideal in the natural lattice of order-bounded [MATH]-module homomorphisms. On this operator lattice the order operations remain [MATH]-strongly bounded and the adjoint is an order automorphism. We then compare the two moduli and explain why they may differ.
tldr: The paper studies adjoints of linear strongly bounded operators on conditional l^2(T) spaces, comparing Riesz–Kantorovich order moduli with spectral moduli and characterizing regular operators as a Dedekind-complete order ideal.
motivation: The work aims to clarify how the Hilbert-type geometry of a conditional space interacts with its Riesz-space order structure, and to understand when natural operator moduli coincide or differ.
method: Purely functional-analytic techniques are used: isolating the C-regular operators, embedding them in the lattice of order-bounded module homomorphisms, and analyzing order operations and adjoints on this lattice.
result: C-regular operators form a Dedekind-complete order ideal, order operations remain strongly bounded, the adjoint acts as an order automorphism, and the two moduli (Riesz–Kantorovich order modulus vs. spectral modulus) are compared with conditions explaining their possible divergence.
conclusion: The paper contributes to abstract operator theory and Riesz-space geometry rather than to any quantum-information, thermodynamic, networking, or hybrid-platform context.

title: A Hybrid Iterative Deep Ritz Method For Elliptic Interface Problems
authors: Tianhao Hu, Bangti Jin, Fengru Wang, Yifeng Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we propose a hybrid iterative deep Ritz method (H-IDRM) for a class of interface problems for second-order elliptic operators. It is based on a new mixed formulation of the problem and involves solving a sequence of convex minimization problems. We employ a level-set neural network architecture, featuring a level-set representation of the interface, to accommodate the piecewise smoothness of the solution and the flux. The approach involves only volumetric representations instead of duality pairing on the interface and avoids explicit interface sampling that is inconvenient for complex interface geometries. Further, we present an analysis of the method, including the errors arising from the neural network approximation, Monte Carlo approximation, iterative scheme, and penalty parameters. Numerical experiments indicate that the H-IDRM outperforms existing neural solvers on problems with high-dimensional domains, intricate interface geometries, and lower subdomain regularity.
tldr: The paper introduces a hybrid iterative deep Ritz method (H-IDRM) for solving second-order elliptic interface problems using level-set neural networks and a new mixed formulation.
motivation: Classical numerical solvers struggle with interface problems featuring high-dimensional domains, complex interface geometries, and low subdomain regularity, motivating neural-network-based PDE solvers.
method: The approach uses a convex-minimization mixed formulation combined with a level-set neural network architecture that encodes the interface implicitly, avoiding explicit interface sampling and duality pairing on the interface, and includes error analysis covering network, Monte Carlo, iterative, and penalty errors.
result: Numerical experiments show that H-IDRM outperforms existing neural solvers on problems with high-dimensional domains, intricate interface geometries, and lower subdomain regularity.
conclusion: The hybrid iterative deep Ritz method offers an effective and theoretically analyzed neural solver for challenging elliptic interface problems in scientific computing.

title: Exact Collision Vertex For Stress And Heat Flux
authors: Ilya Karlin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation, we derive an exact nonlinear generating vertex for collisional stress and heat-flux production. The complete two-input Hermite hierarchy for stress resums to a universal traceless tensor times one scalar radial law, while the heat-flux vertex follows from the same law by an exact contraction. Taylor differentiation yields universal bilinear collision tensors with exact stress and heat-flux gradings, without a finite moment closure. DSMC tests, including wall-driven flows and a bimodal Mach-5 shock, recover independently sampled Boltzmann productions and the predicted convergence, while the converged production is independent of the thermal Gaussian foot used for its Hermite representation.
tldr: The paper derives an exact nonlinear collision vertex for stress and heat-flux production in the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation, yielding universal bilinear collision tensors without finite moment closure.
motivation: To provide a universal and exact description of collisional stress and heat-flux production in kinetic theory, avoiding approximations from moment closure.
method: Uses the Hermite hierarchy and Taylor differentiation to derive the complete two-input generating vertex, validated by DSMC simulations of wall-driven flows and a Mach-5 shock.
result: The two-input Hermite hierarchy resums to a universal traceless tensor times a scalar radial law, with exact stress and heat-flux gradings, and the converged production is independent of the thermal Gaussian foot.
conclusion: The exact collision vertex offers a closure-free approach to stress and heat-flux production, with DSMC tests confirming predicted convergence and independence from Hermite representation details.

title: Metalens-transparent Ultrasound Transducer Module For Extended Depth Photoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Krishnendu Samanta, Myunghoo Lee, Shubham Mirg, Zhihao Zhou, Saniya Patil, Johannes E. Fr\"och, Arka Majumdar, Sri-Rajasekhar Kothapalli
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical-resolution photoacoustic microscopy (ORPAM) provides label-free optical-absorption contrast at millimeter-scale tissue depths with micrometer-scale lateral resolution. However, its volumetric coverage is limited by the short depth of focus of conventional optical lenses, whereas system miniaturization is constrained by bulky optics and ultrasound transducers. Here, we present an extended-depth ORPAM system that combines an ultra-thin metalens for optical excitation with a planar transparent ultrasound transducer (TUT) for photoacoustic detection. Fabricated from piezoelectric lithium niobate, the chip-scale TUT provides ~80% optical transparency and enables coaxial optical excitation with simultaneous acoustic detection at 14.4 MHz center frequency. This architecture eliminates the need for bulky acousto-optic combiners and large-volume acoustic coupling arrangements between the transducer and imaging target. We evaluate three ultra-thin metalens designs as hyperbolic, quadratic, and extended depth-of-focus (EDOF), which provide effective axial ranges of 0.3, 0.8, and 1.3 mm, respectively, with lateral resolutions of 1.1 micron for hyperbolic, 1.2 micron quadratic lenses, and 1.5 micron for EDOF across the full axial range. Phantom experiments demonstrate improved visualization of multilayered, inclined, volumetrically distributed targets with the EDOF design compared with the two other metalenses. Label-free imaging in awake, head-fixed mice further demonstrates that EDOF provides extended-depth visualization of subcortical microvasculature without being subjected to anesthesia-induced confounds. This chip-scale metalens-TUT architecture provides a foundation for developing compact photoacoustic microscopy systems.
tldr: A chip-scale metalens plus transparent ultrasound transducer module enables extended-depth optical-resolution photoacoustic microscopy with improved volumetric imaging of subcortical microvasculature in awake mice.
motivation: Optical-resolution photoacoustic microscopy offers label-free absorption contrast at micrometer resolution, but its volumetric coverage is limited by the short depth of focus of conventional lenses, while miniaturization is restricted by bulky optics and ultrasound transducers.
method: The authors combine an ultra-thin metalens for optical excitation with a planar lithium niobate transparent ultrasound transducer (~80% optical transparency, 14.4 MHz center frequency) for coaxial photoacoustic detection, and compare hyperbolic, quadratic, and extended depth-of-focus (EDOF) metalens designs.
result: The three metalenses provide axial ranges of 0.3, 0.8, and 1.3 mm with lateral resolutions of 1.1, 1.2, and 1.5 microns respectively; phantom and in vivo awake mouse experiments show the EDOF design gives extended-depth visualization of multilayered, inclined, and subcortical targets.
conclusion: The chip-scale metalens-TUT architecture provides a foundation for compact photoacoustic microscopy systems, eliminating bulky acousto-optic combiners and large acoustic coupling volumes.

title: Heun Spectrum, Threshold Hierarchy, And One-Loop Quantum Mass Of The Christ--Lee Kink
authors: Mulyanto, Afif Jalu Pradipta, Ardian Nata Atmaja, Bobby Eka Gunara
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the fluctuation spectrum and renormalized one-loop quantum mass of the Christ--Lee kink over the full positive range of its deformation parameter. The fluctuation equation is reduced exactly to general-Heun form, yielding parity-resolved continuum solutions and implicit quantization conditions for the discrete spectrum. At the first nontrivial continuum crossing, the odd Heun solution truncates to a polynomial, giving the exact threshold \(\epsilon_1=-1}\). For small deformation, the kink separates into two widely spaced \(\phi^6\)-like interfaces and the fluctuation operator develops a long central cavity. This geometry explains the logarithmic growth of the bound-state count, the asymptotically geometric hierarchy of continuum-threshold crossings, and the emergence of a soft relative-translation mode. In the opposite limit, the spectrum approaches the \(\phi^4\) P\"oschl--Teller problem, while its even threshold resonance becomes a shallow bound state at finite deformation. The one-loop correction is evaluated in a fixed vacuum-normal-ordering prescription using a common-regulator spectral trace and independently through an imaginary-frequency functional determinant. The two calculations agree throughout representative finite deformations and reproduce the exact \(\phi^4\) limit. In the small-deformation regime, the extended central region produces a logarithmically enhanced negative quantum correction. These results provide a unified analytic and numerical description of how the spectral reorganization of the Christ--Lee kink controls its semiclassical quantum mass.
tldr: The paper analytically and numerically studies the fluctuation spectrum and one-loop quantum mass of the Christ-Lee kink by mapping its stability equation to general Heun form.
motivation: Understanding how spectral reorganization in deformed kink models controls semiclassical quantum corrections is relevant for soliton quantum field theory.
method: The fluctuation equation is reduced to general-Heun form, yielding parity-resolved continuum solutions and implicit quantization conditions; the one-loop correction is computed via a common-regulator spectral trace and an imaginary-frequency functional determinant.
result: The analysis gives exact thresholds, a geometric hierarchy of continuum-threshold crossings, a soft relative-translation mode, and a logarithmically enhanced negative quantum correction in the small-deformation regime.
conclusion: The Christ-Lee kink provides a unified analytic and numerical description of how spectral reorganization controls its semiclassical quantum mass, connecting to both phi^6-like and phi^4 limits.

title: Anisometric Dielectric Snowman-Particle Provides Improved Control Over Photonic Hook
authors: Yu. E. Geints, I. V. Minin, O. V. Minin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A novel efficient method for controlling photonic hook (PH) with an anisotropic dielectric microparticle dimer in the snowman-particle configuration is introduced and numerically justified. In contrast to existing schemes that rely on structured illumination, partial shielding, or complex morphologies, the proposed anisometric geometry utilizes a simple and easily manufacturable form composed of two partially overlapping cylinders. The finite element method was employed to study how the degree of asymmetry, spatial rotation, and optical properties of the upper particle (the head of the snowman-particle) affect the bending angle and maximum intensity of PH. For the first time, it has been demonstrated that adjusting these parameters allows for the deliberate switching between single and double PH modes, as well as controlling the direction and curvature of the hook, including the fragmentation of the focal area. This approach offers high efficiency in utilizing incident radiation, simplicity in fabrication, and broad tunability of PH characteristics. The findings pave the way for the development of compact near-field optical devices, such as optical traps, high-resolution microscopes, sensors, and tools for surface microstructuring.
tldr: The paper proposes and numerically demonstrates control of photonic hooks using an anisometric dielectric snowman-shaped dimer particle.
motivation: Existing photonic-hook control schemes rely on structured illumination, partial shielding, or complex morphologies, motivating a simpler and more manufacturable geometry.
method: Finite element method simulations are used to study how asymmetry, spatial rotation, and optical properties of the upper particle affect bending angle, maximum intensity, and mode structure.
result: Adjusting the anisometric parameters enables switching between single and double photonic hook modes, controlling hook direction and curvature, and even fragmenting the focal area.
conclusion: The snowman-particle design offers efficient radiation use, simple fabrication, and broad tunability for compact near-field optical devices such as traps, microscopes, and sensors.

title: A Diagrammatic Presentation For Every Pivotal Pointed Fusion Category
authors: Anup Poudel Chumeng Di
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a generators and relations presentation of pivotal pointed fusion categories, [MATH]. Unlike the well-known skeletal model, our presentation is strict and allows multiple isomorphic objects. Our main tool is skein theory, which allows us to apply topological tools to understand the relations of morphisms in the category.
tldr: The paper provides a strict generators-and-relations presentation of pivotal pointed fusion categories using skein theory, allowing multiple isomorphic objects rather than the usual skeletal model.
motivation: Pivotal pointed fusion categories are typically studied via skeletal models, which restrict to one object per isomorphism class and may obscure structural relations. A strict presentation that permits multiple isomorphic objects could offer a more flexible framework for diagrammatic reasoning.
method: The authors employ skein theory to construct a diagrammatic calculus for morphisms in pivotal pointed fusion categories. This allows topological tools to be applied to derive generators and relations.
result: They obtain a complete generators-and-relations presentation for every pivotal pointed fusion category, generalizing beyond the skeletal approach.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that skein-theoretic methods yield a strict diagrammatic presentation for this class of fusion categories, potentially simplifying computations and connecting to topological invariants.

title: Shape Without Scale: An Identifiability Dichotomy For A Bounded Tail Observed Through A Non-additive Measurement Kernel
authors: Jiarui Qi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A latent severity has a bounded lower tail with density of shape alpha and scale L. It is observed only through a fixed Markov kernel K that is biased and non-additive. The relative conditional spread of K diverges at the endpoint. Our sample is i.i.d. from the marginal Q alone, with no anchoring covariate or instrument. We prove a dichotomy. The shape index alpha is identifiable: for every admissible choice of the class constants, any two observationally equivalent members of a lean class share alpha, determined by a near-endpoint expansion of Q. The rate, namely L and the fixed-scale exceedance p_tau, does not survive. There exist admissible shared class constants and two members of a smaller regularity class whose observed laws coincide exactly. Across the pair alpha agrees, whereas L and p_tau move. A degenerate Le Cam two-point bound excludes any uniformly consistent estimator of either, and pointwise consistency fails at one member. Only the rate needs an anchor. We conjecture that a known kernel family with known edge map identifies the rate fiber by fiber if and only if the family satisfies a fixed-scale injectivity clause, and we prove the sufficiency direction. In surrogate safety, uncalibrated conflict data give the shape of near-crash risk, not its absolute rate.
tldr: The paper proves an identifiability dichotomy for a bounded-tail latent severity observed through a biased, non-additive Markov kernel: the tail shape is identifiable while the scale-rate parameters are not, unless an anchoring instrument is available.
motivation: The work is motivated by settings such as surrogate safety, where uncalibrated conflict data may reveal the shape of near-crash risk but not its absolute rate due to biased, lossy observation mechanisms.
method: The authors analyze an i.i.d. sample from the marginal observation law Q induced by a fixed Markov kernel K with divergent relative conditional spread at the endpoint, proving a dichotomy via near-endpoint expansions and a degenerate Le Cam two-point lower bound.
result: The shape index alpha is identifiable from Q, whereas the scale L and fixed-scale exceedance p_tau are not; no uniformly consistent estimator exists for either non-identifiable rate parameter, and pointwise consistency fails at one member of the constructed pair.
conclusion: Only the rate requires an anchor; the authors conjecture and partially prove that a known kernel family with a fixed-scale injectivity clause identifies the rate fiber by fiber, clarifying what can and cannot be learned from uncalibrated surrogate data.

title: Distributed Stochastic Approximation Algorithms And Heavy-Tailed Age Of Information
authors: Adrian Redder, Arunselvan Ramaswamy, Holger Karl
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Algorithms in multi-agent systems such as federated learning, mobile robotic swarming, and consensus control can be designed and analyzed as distributed stochastic approximation algorithms. Such algorithms involve information exchanges between agents for various computations. The freshness of the information can be quantified using the Age of Information (AoI) metric. Consider robotic teams operating in highly obstructed geographical settings, such as subterranean or dense urban environments. Because of spatial disconnections, AoI has empirically been observed to be heavy-tailed with unbounded moments. However, most analyses assume AoI with bounded moments, creating a gap between theory and practice. To the best of our knowledge, ours is the first analysis under general heavy-tailed AoI with potentially infinite mean. We study the stability (almost sure boundedness of the distributed iterates) and convergence of multi-agent systems that are strictly dissipative in the scaling limit (system at ``infinity''). Examples include most gradient-based and consensus algorithms under the Robbins-Monro step-size regime.
tldr: This paper analyzes stability and convergence of distributed stochastic approximation algorithms in multi-agent systems under heavy-tailed Age of Information with possibly infinite mean.
motivation: Multi-agent systems such as robotic swarms and federated learning rely on information exchange, but existing analyses often assume bounded AoI moments, whereas practical obstructed environments produce heavy-tailed AoI.
method: The authors study distributed stochastic approximation algorithms that are strictly dissipative in the scaling limit and derive almost-sure boundedness and convergence under general heavy-tailed AoI using Robbins-Monro step sizes.
result: They provide the first analysis of distributed stochastic approximation under heavy-tailed AoI with potentially infinite mean, extending stability and convergence guarantees beyond prior bounded-moment assumptions.
conclusion: The work bridges theory and practice for multi-agent systems in spatially disconnected settings, but it is purely classical and does not engage quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Block Erasure Channel And Block z-Channel With Bounded Decoders And Finite Blocklength
authors: Bin Han, Yao Zhu, Rafael F. Schaefer, Wenwen Chen, Giuseppe Caire, Anke Schmeink, H. Vincent Poor, Hans D. Schotten
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Block error rate is a standard metric in finite blocklength (FBL) communication, yet it conflates two qualitatively different failure modes: block confusions, where the decoder selects a wrong codeword, and block erasures, where it declares a loss. Higher-layer protocols treat physical-layer failures as erasures, but this cross-layer assumption lacks FBL justification. We derive a rigorous upper bound and a companion lower-side estimate on the block confusion probability (BLCP) and block erasure probability (BLEP) for bounded-distance decoders over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels at finite blocklength, recasting the coding problem as a geometric sphere packing one. We analyze the sensitivity of these bounds to blocklength and signalto-noise ratio, characterize the envelope of the upper bound, and derive closed-form Chernoff approximations. Extending the model to idle transmission blocks, we bound the false alarm probability (FAP) and show that a block z-channel abstraction emerges from the bounded-decoding geometry. Numerical results confirm that confusion and false alarm probabilities lie far below the error rate constraint, providing quantitative physicallayer support for the block erasure channel and block z-channel abstractions assumed in protocol design.
tldr: The paper derives finite-blocklength bounds on block confusion and erasure probabilities for bounded-distance decoders over AWGN channels, supporting block erasure and block z-channel abstractions.
motivation: Higher-layer protocols often treat physical-layer failures as erasures, but this cross-layer assumption lacks finite-blocklength justification.
method: The coding problem is recast as geometric sphere packing to derive upper and lower bounds on block confusion and erasure probabilities, including Chernoff approximations and extension to idle transmission blocks.
result: The bounds characterize sensitivity to blocklength and SNR, show that confusion and false alarm probabilities lie far below the error rate constraint, and yield a block z-channel abstraction.
conclusion: The work provides quantitative physical-layer support for block erasure and block z-channel models assumed in protocol design.

title: Multi-View Fusion For Encrypted C2 Detection: A Leakage-Controlled Measurement Study Of Evaluation Pitfalls
authors: Hoang-Huy Nguyen-Huu, Van-Tri Phan, Khuong Nguyen-An
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Command-and-control (C2) traffic increasingly hides within TLS, so defenders now apply machine learning to traffic metadata. Many studies assume that combining two metadata views, namely flow statistics and TLS handshake fingerprints, improves both accuracy and robustness. We tested this assumption on 17,577 TLS flows from 62 real Cobalt Strike captures. Our evaluation removes the data leakage that leads to overly optimistic reported scores. We report three findings that matter more than the fusion result itself. First, an incorrect preprocessing step increases the F1 score by 0.28. This step computes the frequency encoding across the entire dataset rather than within each cross-validation fold. The increase is about ten times larger than any real effect we measured. Second, both the labels and the behavioral features depend on the destination address. Because of this, the 17,577 flows form only 2,132 independent groups, and the positive rate of 55.1\%, which looks balanced, drops to 4.2\%. Therefore, class balance is just a result of how we analyze the data, specifically whether we count flows or endpoints, and not a real feature of the task. Third, 20 of the 62 captures (32\%) have no TLS flows to any known C2 address, so they contain only benign samples. We checked these captures directly and confirmed that this is a gap in the ground truth, not a labeling error. In this context, fusion beats the best single view by only 0.022 in F1. When an attacker forges both feature surfaces simultaneously, every model performs worse than a simple baseline that always predicts positive (F1 = 0.711). For encrypted C2 detection, the evaluation design is not a preliminary step. It the main result.
tldr: A leakage-controlled re-evaluation of machine-learning-based encrypted command-and-control (C2) traffic detection shows that fusion of flow-statistics and TLS-handshake views yields only marginal gains, while evaluation design dominates reported performance.
motivation: Many studies assume that combining multiple metadata views (flow statistics plus TLS handshake fingerprints) improves encrypted C2 detection accuracy and robustness, but these claims may be inflated by data leakage and flawed evaluation design.
method: Using 17,577 TLS flows from 62 real Cobalt Strike captures, the authors systematically remove leakage sources — fold-external frequency encoding, destination-address-induced label/feature dependence (2,132 independent groups), and ground-truth gaps in 20 captures with only benign samples — and retrain multi-view and single-view classifiers under clean cross-validation.
result: Incorrect dataset-wide frequency encoding inflates F1 by 0.28 (roughly 10x any real effect); accounting for grouping drops the apparent positive rate from 55.1% to 4.2%; and proper fusion beats the best single view by only 0.022 F1, with all models falling below a trivial always-positive baseline (F1 = 0.711) under adversarial forgery of both feature surfaces.
conclusion: For encrypted C2 detection, evaluation design is not a preliminary step but the main result; reported fusion benefits are largely artifacts of leakage and endpoint-vs-flow counting choices.

title: Coloring Queens With Thousands Of Encodings
authors: Bernardo Subercaseaux, Benjamin Przybocki, Marijn J. H. Heule
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In The Art of Computer Programming, Knuth benchmarked 10 encoding techniques for computing the chromatic number of the queen's graph: the minimum number of colors needed to color the squares of an [MATH] chessboard so that no two squares sharing a row, column, or diagonal receive the same color. In this paper, we extend his analysis much further by comparing thousands of encodings for the same problem, which allows us to identify additional factors that are important for solver performance. We obtain 1584 encodings for this problem by varying (a) the constraints that encode which color is assigned to each cell, (b) the constraints that forbid the same color appearing in a row, column, or diagonal line, and (c) the symmetry-breaking constraints. We find that the three most impactful encoding factors are (i) the choice of symmetry-breaking constraints, (ii) enabling so-called clique hints, and (iii) enforcing that each cell is assigned exactly one color through blocked clauses. Furthermore, while Knuth proposed clique hints as an advantage of the order encoding, we show in fact that they can be effectively employed for the one-hot encoding as well.
tldr: A large-scale empirical comparison of thousands of SAT/CP encoding variants for computing the chromatic number of the queen's graph, identifying symmetry-breaking constraints, clique hints, and blocked-clause exactly-one encodings as the most impactful factors.
motivation: Knuth benchmarked only 10 encodings for the queen's graph coloring problem, leaving open which encoding choices drive SAT solver performance. The authors aim to systematically explore a much larger encoding space to isolate the decisive factors.
method: They generate 1584 encodings by varying (a) cell-color assignment constraints, (b) line-based conflict constraints, and (c) symmetry-breaking constraints, then benchmark solver performance across these configurations and analyze the impact of each factor, including transferring clique hints from order encoding to one-hot encoding.
result: The three most impactful factors are the choice of symmetry-breaking constraints, the use of clique hints, and enforcing exactly-one-color-per-cell via blocked clauses; clique hints, previously thought specific to order encoding, also prove effective for one-hot encoding.
conclusion: Encoding design choices substantially affect combinatorial solver performance, and their systematic benchmarking methodology yields generalizable guidance for formulating graph-coloring and related combinatorial problems as SAT instances.

title: Trouble At The Top: Can Python Extend The Chains Of Trust In Infrastructure Firmware?
authors: Sergey Bratus Larry Hernandez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compiled Python bytecode (PYC) has become an essential part of network switches, routers, and other network infrastructure devices. Our analysis shows that its integrity is implicitly trusted in multiple designs that make use of Python code at the top of the operational software, such as the management and control pane of enterprise network switches. At the same time, the integrity of PYC files is not covered under the traditional chain-of-trust models, due to complex interactions with the CPython loader, byte compiler, and other Python runtime components. We explore the risks inherent in including PYC and Python runtimes in the de facto trusted code basis of commercial enterprise equipment and offer a comprehensive framework for understanding emergent behaviors in these designs.
tldr: The paper analyzes the implicit trust placed in compiled Python bytecode (PYC) and Python runtimes within enterprise network infrastructure firmware, showing these components escape traditional chain-of-trust models.
motivation: Network switches, routers, and other infrastructure devices increasingly rely on Python at the management and control planes, yet the integrity of PYC files is not covered by conventional trusted-computing bases, creating an under-examined security risk.
method: The authors examine how PYC files interact with the CPython loader, byte compiler, and other runtime components, and analyze multiple commercial design patterns that implicitly trust Python code at the top of the operational software stack.
result: They identify concrete integrity gaps where malicious or corrupted PYC can subvert the software trust chain, and propose a framework for reasoning about emergent behaviors in these designs.
conclusion: Securing infrastructure firmware requires extending chain-of-trust models to cover Python runtimes and bytecode, since current assumptions leave a significant and largely unaddressed attack surface.

title: Percolation In The Stochastic Block Model
authors: Luca Pieleanu, Moritz Laber, Narayan G. Sabhahit, Dmitri Krioukov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The stochastic block model is a paradigmatic model of networks with community structure. Yet percolation in the model has been studied primarily in cases with a fixed block structure, even though in real networks, the community structure may evolve as the network grows. Here we study percolation in sequences of stochastic block models in which the numbers and sizes of communities, as well as the intra- and intercommunity connection probabilities may all change with the network size. We analyze five such sequences using two methods: linearized self-consistent equations for the locally tree-like models and a branching process at the community scale for the models with nonvanishing clustering. We find that the critical average degree is not generally equal to [MATH], even in locally tree-like sequences, because the transition depends on how connections are distributed across the evolving community structure. We also show that the community-scale branching process accurately predicts the transition when intercommunity connections are sufficiently sparse, even in the presence of nonvanishing clustering, while a geometric stochastic block model sequence demonstrates the limitations of this method when correlations between intercommunity connections cannot be neglected. These results extend percolation studies in the stochastic block model to more realistic scenarios with evolving community structure, and may provide new methods to derive the upper and lower bounds for the percolation threshold in geometric long-range percolation.
tldr: The paper studies percolation in sequences of stochastic block models with evolving community structure, showing that the critical average degree depends on how connections are distributed across communities.
motivation: Real networks often have community structures that evolve as the network grows, but percolation in stochastic block models has mostly been studied with fixed block structure.
method: The authors analyze five sequences of stochastic block models using linearized self-consistent equations for locally tree-like models and a community-scale branching process for models with nonvanishing clustering.
result: They find that the critical average degree is not generally equal to the standard value even for locally tree-like sequences, and the branching process predicts the transition accurately when intercommunity connections are sparse, but fails for geometric models with strong correlations.
conclusion: These results extend percolation studies in stochastic block models to more realistic evolving community structures and may inform bounds for geometric long-range percolation.

title: Algebraically Primitive Teichm\"uller Curves In \Omega\mathcal M_g(2g-2)^{\mathrm{hyp}}
authors: Myeongjae Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a complete classification of algebraically primitive Teichm\"uller curves in [MATH] for [MATH]. They are precisely the curves generated by the double regular \((2g+1)\)-gon when \(2g+1\) is prime, and by the regular \(4g\)-gon when \(g\) is a power of two.
tldr: The paper classifies algebraically primitive Teichmüller curves in a specific stratum of moduli space, showing they arise from double regular (2g+1)-gons and regular 4g-gons under number-theoretic conditions.
motivation: Teichmüller curves are important geometric objects connecting dynamics on moduli spaces, algebraic geometry, and number theory, but their classification in higher genus strata remains largely open.
method: The author uses techniques from Teichmüller dynamics, translation surfaces, and algebraic geometry to study and completely classify algebraically primitive Teichmüller curves in the hyperelliptic locus ΩM_g(2g−2)^hyp.
result: The classification states that the algebraically primitive Teichmüller curves are precisely those generated by the double regular (2g+1)-gon when 2g+1 is prime, and by the regular 4g-gon when g is a power of two.
conclusion: This provides a complete classification for the specified stratum, advancing the understanding of primitive Teichmüller curves and their connection to regular polygons, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Truncation Bands, Unitality, And Homomorphisms In Truncated Riesz Spaces: Boulabiar's Problems And Beyond
authors: Hamza Hafsi Mohamed Habibi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We answer three questions from Boulabiar's survey on truncated Riesz spaces. First, the truncation band projection property coincides with the principal projection property, with no completeness or Archimedean hypothesis needed, and the band projection onto a truncation band is then given explicitly by the truncation itself. Second, a truncation on any Riesz space is unital exactly when its fixed-point set has a supremum. Hence bounded truncations on [MATH]-spaces are unital, and a nonunital truncated Banach lattice with bounded truncation contains a closed sublattice copy of [MATH] and is never an [MATH]-space, while on the [MATH] side the smallest truncation unitization norm is always an [MATH]-norm, though the largest one need not be. Third, a truncation homomorphism whose domain truncation is Archimedean need not be a Riesz homomorphism, as an explicit counterexample built from [MATH] and [MATH] shows, but it is one modulo truncation infinitesimals whenever the codomain space is Archimedean.
tldr: This pure mathematics paper resolves three open problems in Boulabiar's survey on truncated Riesz spaces, characterizing truncation band projections, unitality conditions, and truncation homomorphisms.
motivation: Boulabiar's survey left several structural questions open regarding truncated Riesz spaces, including the relationship between truncation band projection and principal projection properties, the characterization of unital truncations, and whether truncation homomorphisms must be Riesz homomorphisms.
method: The authors work within the abstract order-theoretic framework of Riesz spaces and Banach lattices, proving equivalence theorems and constructing explicit counterexamples (e.g., from C(K) and c0-type spaces) to settle the homomorphism question.
result: They show the truncation band projection property equals the principal projection property without completeness or Archimedean assumptions, that a truncation is unital exactly when its fixed-point set has a supremum, and that truncation homomorphisms are Riesz homomorphisms only modulo truncation infinitesimals when the codomain is Archimedean.
conclusion: The paper settles three of Boulabiar's problems and provides new structural results on unitization norms for truncated Banach lattices, but remains entirely within abstract order theory with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Rolling Conformal Prediction In Sequential Model Training
authors: Chen Cheng, Ruiting Liang, Rina Foygel Barber
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Rolling Conformal Prediction (rolling-CP), a distribution-free predictive inference method for the setting of sequential model training. Specifically, given a data stream [MATH], at each time [MATH] the trained model may depend on the observed history [MATH]. This setting arises naturally in modern sequential training, including one-pass training over massive datasets and continual fine-tuning or test-time adaptation of language models during deployment. Rolling-CP first calibrates each incoming observation against the current predictor and then rolls it into future training. In this way, we avoid the need for data splitting.
