Remarkably, although the models at times [MATH] may have entirely different properties and accuracy levels, for exchangeable data it is nonetheless possible to establish a guarantee of marginal coverage, with a familiar universal factor-two guarantee (a worst case guarantee of [MATH] coverage, as compared to the target level [MATH]), without any assumptions of stability or any restrictions on the model training process. For i.i.d. data streams, we further prove high-probability training-conditional validity uniformly over time; under stability conditions, coverage guarantees sharpen towards [MATH]. Numerical experiments on sequential regression, multiclass SGD, and one-pass neural-network training further demonstrate the practical effectiveness of rolling-CP.
tldr: Rolling Conformal Prediction provides distribution-free predictive inference for sequentially trained models without data splitting.
motivation: Modern sequential training and continual test-time adaptation require valid uncertainty quantification, but standard conformal prediction methods rely on data splitting and stable models.
method: The method calibrates each incoming observation against the current predictor and then rolls it into future training, avoiding data splitting. It establishes marginal coverage guarantees and, for i.i.d. streams, high-probability training-conditional validity uniformly over time.
result: For exchangeable data, a universal factor-two marginal coverage guarantee holds without stability assumptions, and under stability conditions coverage sharpens toward the target level. Experiments on sequential regression, multiclass SGD, and one-pass neural-network training demonstrate effectiveness.
conclusion: Rolling-CP offers a practical and theoretically grounded approach to distribution-free inference in evolving model training settings, though it is outside quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Local Optimality And Rigidity Of Frobenius Tests For Dense High-Dimensional Covariance Alternatives
authors: Peter Reinhard Hansen, Werner Ploberger, Chen Tong
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study identity testing for high-dimensional covariance matrices against dense alternatives of unknown direction, with [MATH]. Along a globally positive quadratic precision path, mixing Gaussian alternatives over a Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble direction yields a contiguous experiment whose log likelihood reduces to the corrected Frobenius statistic; its upper-tail test attains the limiting weighted-power envelope at every fixed strength. Fixing the prior's Frobenius radius perturbs the mixture by only [MATH] in total variation, and exact whitening carries the experiment, the statistic, and its null law to any known null covariance. Separately, under a product-coordinate null, feasibility needs only [MATH] moments, plus identical distributions over time when means are estimated; studentization and an exact degrees-of-freedom correction preserve the local power. A stability inequality turns near-envelope attainment into null agreement with the Frobenius rule, so uniform noninferiority on the typical dense bulk precludes gains at any contiguous alternative. For trace-matched rank-one alternatives, the corrected statistic is the first likelihood direction when [MATH] and [MATH]; at fixed strength, the log likelihood ratio in the Onatski-Moreira-Hallin fixed-spike benchmark is governed by a richer linear spectral statistic below the Baik-Ben Arous-Peche threshold, while eigenvalue separation permits cost-free largest-eigenvalue enhancement above it. Simulations illustrate the theory.
tldr: This paper studies local optimality and rigidity of corrected Frobenius tests for high-dimensional covariance identity testing against dense alternatives of unknown direction.
motivation: High-dimensional covariance testing against dense alternatives lacks a clear understanding of the power limits and optimality properties of Frobenius-type statistics.
method: The authors construct a contiguous Gaussian mixture experiment over Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble directions, reduce its log-likelihood to the corrected Frobenius statistic, and use a stability inequality plus spectral benchmark analysis.
result: They show the Frobenius test attains the limiting weighted-power envelope locally, is rigid under typical dense-bulk noninferiority, and characterizes a richer linear spectral statistic below the Baik-Ben Arous-Peche threshold.
conclusion: Frobenius tests are locally optimal and rigid for dense high-dimensional covariance alternatives, with precise implications for uniform noninferiority and fixed-spike benchmarks.

title: Mesoscopic Redundancy For Dynamical Frames Generated By Atomic Singular Model Operators
authors: Javad Mashreghi Ilya Krishtal
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the compressed shift [MATH] on [MATH] associated with the atomic singular inner function [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH]. Let [MATH] and define real powers [MATH] using a holomorphic logarithm near the singleton spectrum of [MATH]. For any temporal multisequence [MATH] with uniformly bounded numbers of samples in unit intervals, we prove that [MATH] is a frame if and only if [MATH] is Kummer-thick: the frequencies [MATH], weighted by [MATH], have uniformly positive total mass in every sufficiently distant interval of some fixed length. Equivalently, the occupied unit cells fill a fixed positive proportion of every window [MATH] for some [MATH] and all sufficiently large [MATH]. The proof combines a Volterra transmutation into Bessel waves with the Fourier--Bessel Logvinenko--Sereda theorem.
tldr: The paper characterizes when certain dynamical frames generated by atomic singular model operators are frames, linking the frame property to a Kummer-thick condition on frequencies.
motivation: To understand redundancy and frame properties for shift-invariant spaces associated with atomic singular inner functions, a problem in operator theory and sampling.
method: Combines a Volterra transmutation into Bessel waves with the Fourier–Bessel Logvinenko–Sereda theorem to analyze the frame condition.
result: Proves that the frame property is equivalent to the frequencies being Kummer-thick, meaning they have uniformly positive total mass in every sufficiently distant interval of fixed length.
conclusion: Provides a characterization of frame redundancy for these operators, with potential implications for sampling theory in model spaces.

title: Maximal Monotone Differential Inclusions With Volterra And One-Sided Lipschitz Perturbations Under Nonlocal Initial Conditions And Applications
authors: Torres-Valdebenito Manuel Jourani Abderrahim
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a class of differential inclusions governed by non-autonomous and autonomous maximal monotone operators, involving set-valued perturbations with a Volterra integral term and subject to a nonlocal condition. Under suitable assumptions on the governing operator, the set-valued perturbation, and the Volterra kernel, we establish existence results for solutions. In particular, the set-valued perturbation is assumed to satisfy a one-sided Lipschitz condition, while the Volterra kernel is required to be Lipschitz continuous. The existence of a trajectory is established by means of an iterative construction and an application of Zorn's lemma. Finally, several examples are presented to illustrate the applicability of the abstract results.
tldr: This paper studies the existence of solutions for a class of differential inclusions driven by maximal monotone operators with Volterra integral terms and one-sided Lipschitz set-valued perturbations under nonlocal initial conditions.
motivation: The authors aim to extend existence theory for non-autonomous and autonomous maximal monotone differential inclusions to settings that simultaneously involve Volterra integral perturbations, one-sided Lipschitz set-valued maps, and nonlocal initial conditions.
method: Existence of trajectories is proven using an iterative construction combined with an application of Zorn's lemma, under assumptions of one-sided Lipschitz continuity on the set-valued perturbation and Lipschitz continuity of the Volterra kernel.
result: Existence results for solutions are established for both non-autonomous and autonomous maximal monotone operators with Volterra and one-sided Lipschitz perturbations, and several illustrative examples demonstrate the applicability of the abstract framework.
conclusion: The work provides a general existence theory for a broad class of nonlinear differential inclusions with nonlocal conditions, though it lies entirely in classical nonlinear functional analysis and has no connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Strong Measurability And Adapted Approximations With Applications To Non-Markovian Control
authors: Jinniao Qiu Keivan Mirzaei
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study strong measurability and adapted approximations for maps taking values in possibly nonseparable metric spaces. After recalling the metric-space Pettis criterion, we give conditions under which measurability implies strong measurability. Under the continuum hypothesis (CH), every measurable map from a countably generated measurable space into a metric space is strongly measurable for every measure on the domain. For finite or [MATH]-finite measures, the same conclusion holds when the target density is strictly smaller than every real-valued measurable cardinal. Under CH this includes targets of density at most [MATH]; if no real-valued measurable cardinal exists, it holds for all metric targets. For function-valued maps, we show that pointwise measurability and continuity of the sections need not ensure measurability in the function-space topology. We provide a verification criterion using countably many evaluations and essential separability of the range. Further, we obtain elementary [MATH]-approximations of progressive or jointly measurable adapted processes under suitable filtration assumptions, Lipschitz functionals with path and Wasserstein variables, and smooth approximations based on finitely many observations of a process with left- or right-continuous paths. Finally, under CH and suitable assumptions, we apply these results to controlled stochastic differential equations in separable Hilbert spaces, allowing for jumps, random coefficients, path dependence, and state- and control-law dependence; we establish convergence of states and costs uniformly over admissible controls, convergence of optimal values, and transfer of near-optimal controls.
tldr: The paper develops strong measurability and adapted approximation results for maps into nonseparable metric spaces and applies them to non-Markovian stochastic control problems.
motivation: Stochastic control with path-, state-, and control-law dependence requires measurable selections and approximations under weak measurability assumptions, especially beyond separable settings.
method: It uses the metric-space Pettis criterion, continuum hypothesis arguments, countably many evaluations, essential separability, Lipschitz functionals of path and Wasserstein variables, and smooth approximations from finitely many observations.
result: It gives conditions under which measurability implies strong measurability, constructs adapted approximations, and proves convergence of states and costs uniformly over admissible controls, along with convergence of optimal values and transfer of near-optimal controls.
conclusion: The work provides a general measurability and approximation framework for controlled stochastic differential equations in Hilbert spaces with jumps, random coefficients, and path- or law-dependent dynamics.

title: Comparative Evaluation Of Static Embedding Models For Http Request Anomaly Detection
authors: Amanda Riverol, Gustavo Betarte, Rodrigo Mart\'inez, \'alvaro Pardo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web applications are increasingly targeted by cyberattacks that exploit HTTP requests to evade security mechanisms. Traditional web application firewalls (WAFs) rely on rule-based approaches that often exhibit high false positive rates and limited adaptability. Recent studies have explored machine learning techniques and word embedding models to improve anomaly detection in HTTP traffic. This paper presents a benchmark for static embedding models, specifically Word2Vec, FastText, and Doc2Vec, within a unified, single-class classification framework. We propose HEDA (HTTP Embedding-Based Detection Architecture), a modular detection pipeline that combines static embedding representations with single-class anomaly detection models to detect anomalies at the request level. The approach operates in an unsupervised environment, where both the embedding models and detectors are trained exclusively on benign HTTP traffic. The proposed methodology is evaluated on three datasets with heterogeneous characteristics, including both synthetic and real traffic. The experimental results show that the choice of embedding representation significantly affects detection performance, and that FastText-based embeds produce the most consistent results across all datasets, achieving high detection rates while keeping false positive rates under control.
tldr: The paper benchmarks static word embedding models (Word2Vec, FastText, Doc2Vec) within a single-class anomaly detection framework for HTTP request-level attack detection.
motivation: Web application firewalls relying on rule-based approaches suffer from high false positive rates and limited adaptability, motivating machine learning methods for HTTP anomaly detection.
method: The authors propose HEDA, a modular pipeline that combines static embeddings with single-class anomaly detectors trained only on benign HTTP traffic, and evaluate on three heterogeneous datasets.
result: FastText-based embeddings consistently achieved high detection rates with controlled false positive rates across all datasets, while performance varied significantly with the choice of embedding model.
conclusion: Static embedding representations materially affect HTTP anomaly detection performance, and FastText offers the most robust option in the unsupervised single-class setting.

title: Acts: A Multi-tier Benchmark Evaluating Llm Cipher Identification Under Controlled Blind Conditions
authors: Mohammed Khalaf Salama Youssef Hamdi Zafaan Ibrahim
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce ACTS (Artifacts in Cipher Testing Suite), a reproducible benchmark that isolates cryptanalytic ability through tiered metadata deprivation (Tier-1: full metadata; Tier-2: filename only; Tier-3: completely blind) and tests forced reasoning (Tier-5: chain-of-thought, code-as-reasoning, self-correction) on ciphertext alone. A 10-configuration ablation study on 7,000 files, using a single 70/30 train-test split for feature-removal analysis, provides additional evidence at scale. Live API inference on a v2b corpus with fully randomised padding (PKCS7, ISO 10126, and ANSI X9.23 selected per file), unique CSPRNG keys, and unique plaintexts (127 files per model, 381 Tier-1 records, 380 Tier-3 records across three cloud systems, supplemented by 254 autonomous agentic evaluations in Tier-4) yields a combined Tier-3 accuracy of 30.8%, only modestly above the 14.3% random baseline for seven-way classification. The corresponding combined metadata-dependency gap is 40.9 percentage points (Tier-1: 71.7% vs. Tier-3: 30.8%). Against a classical Random Forest (69.2% on 7,000 files, trained on engineered byte-level features), the observed live gap is 38.4 percentage points. Because this comparison spans different input representations and training paradigms, the gap should be interpreted as an overall capability difference rather than a clean factorial decomposition. Six findings are reported: (1) Metadata dependency remains large; (2) Scaling failure under blind conditions; (3) Forced reasoning is epiphenomenal; (4) The observed live capability gap exceeds earlier heuristic estimates; (5) The signal is primarily structural rather than statistical; (6) Heuristic invariance versus ML fragility reveals different failure modes.
tldr: ACTS is a benchmark evaluating LLM cipher identification under metadata-deprived and forced-reasoning conditions, showing limited blind cryptanalytic capability compared with metadata-informed and classical ML baselines.
motivation: The authors aim to isolate cryptanalytic ability in large language models by controlling access to metadata and forcing reasoning, addressing hype about LLM capabilities in cryptographic tasks.
method: They introduce tiered metadata deprivation (full metadata, filename-only, blind), forced-reasoning conditions, a 10-configuration ablation on 7,000 files, and live API inference on a randomized v2b corpus with unique keys and plaintexts across multiple cloud systems.
result: Combined Tier-3 accuracy is 30.8%, only modestly above the 14.3% random baseline, with a 40.9 percentage-point metadata-dependency gap; classical Random Forest reaches 69.2%, yielding a 38.4-point live gap.
conclusion: The benchmark indicates that LLM cipher identification remains highly metadata-dependent, scaling fails under blind conditions, forced reasoning is epiphenomenal, and the signal is primarily structural rather than statistical.

title: Reliable Federated TinyML Deployment For IoT Security
authors: Younsoo Park, Seokhyoen Bae, Shasi Kumar Ramachandran Prabhu, Suman Saha, Peilong Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing deployment of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has increased the need for privacy-preserving intrusion detection systems that operate directly on resource-constrained hardware. Federated Learning enables collaborative model training without sharing raw data, but conventional federated models are often too large and unstable for deployment on microcontroller-class devices. TinyML techniques enable compact neural networks but are typically designed for inference-only workloads. This work investigates combining Federated Learning with TinyML-based model compression for intrusion detection in IoT environments. We evaluate compression strategies including knowledge distillation, structured pruning, and quantization within a federated training pipeline. Preliminary results show that training stability plays a critical role in federated TinyML systems. In particular, server-coordinated cosine learning-rate scheduling improves Attack Recall from 46.7% to 93.85% while enabling substantial model compression and efficient edge deployment. These findings provide insights for designing lightweight and privacy preserving intrusion detection systems for IoT devices.
tldr: This paper combines federated learning with TinyML model compression techniques (knowledge distillation, structured pruning, quantization) to build privacy-preserving intrusion detection systems deployable on microcontroller-class IoT devices.
motivation: IoT devices need privacy-preserving intrusion detection that runs on resource-constrained hardware, but standard federated models are too large and unstable for microcontrollers, and existing TinyML methods mostly target inference-only workloads.
method: The authors integrate knowledge distillation, structured pruning, and quantization into a federated training pipeline and evaluate training stability, notably introducing server-coordinated cosine learning-rate scheduling.
result: Server-coordinated cosine learning-rate scheduling raised Attack Recall from 46.7% to 93.85% while still allowing substantial model compression and efficient edge deployment.
conclusion: Training stability is a critical factor in federated TinyML systems, and careful learning-rate coordination enables lightweight, privacy-preserving intrusion detection suitable for IoT edge devices.

title: SoK: You Find What You Seek: Rethinking Oracles, Guidance, And Input Generation In Hardware Fuzzing
authors: G Abarajithan, Zhenghua Ma, Cristian Tirelli, Andres Meza, Francesco Restuccia, Cynthia Sturton, Ryan Kastner
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware fuzzing is an active area in security verification research, yet its industrial adoption remains in its early stages. This SoK examines which lessons from software fuzzing carry over to hardware and where unique approaches are needed. By analyzing 52 fuzzers across RTL/IP, CPU, NoC, and SoC designs, we introduce an analytical framework that frames verification as a bounded search. This search is defined by its objective, oracle, guidance, input generation, target abstraction, and budget. Consequently, a campaign only uncovers failures it can effectively reach, recognize, and prioritize before exhausting its resources. We distinguish two roles for hardware fuzzing: (1) augmenting constrained-random verification (CRV) via feedback-guided coverage and (2) directed adversarial testing based on threat models and security specifications. Through our framework, we identify what each campaign can observe and generate, providing a basis for assessing the evidence behind reported results. Our analysis suggests that mainstream adoption of hardware fuzzing will require reusable interfaces, target-specific verification assets, reproducible evaluations, and transparent reporting of cost and user effort.
tldr: This SoK paper analyzes 52 hardware fuzzers and proposes a framework for hardware fuzzing as bounded search, distinguishing coverage-guided CRV augmentation from directed adversarial testing.
motivation: Hardware fuzzing is active in security verification but lacks industrial adoption; the paper examines which software fuzzing lessons transfer and where hardware-specific approaches are needed.
method: The authors systematically review 52 fuzzers across RTL/IP, CPU, NoC, and SoC designs and introduce an analytical framework characterizing verification campaigns by objective, oracle, guidance, input generation, target abstraction, and budget.
result: The framework reveals what each campaign can observe and generate, identifies two roles for hardware fuzzing, and suggests that mainstream adoption requires reusable interfaces, target-specific assets, reproducible evaluations, and transparent cost/user-effort reporting.
conclusion: Hardware fuzzing remains distinct from software fuzzing and its path to industrial adoption depends on addressing infrastructure, reproducibility, and reporting gaps rather than solely algorithmic advances.

title: Optimal Weighting Of Training Data In Adaptive Coding
authors: Yuriy Reznik
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive coders are commonly primed with training data, turned into context tables or shipped dictionaries. The training data generally do not match the source being encoded, and the coder must decide how much to trust them. We make that trust a design variable: a Krichevsky--Trofimov (KT) estimator over an [MATH]-ary alphabet whose training counts are scaled by [MATH]. For a training sequence of length [MATH] at Kullback--Leibler divergence [MATH] nats per symbol from the message source, the redundancy-minimizing weight is [MATH], [MATH]. The effective training length [MATH] follows a harmonic law: any mismatch caps the usable training information at [MATH] symbols, however much was collected. Three implementable selectors supply the unknown [MATH]: offline, from the spread of the training set; by a plug-in loop, from the decoded prefix; and by a twice-universal mixture, with no estimation at all. On the ten English texts of the Calgary and Canterbury corpora, weighting removes up to [MATH] of the redundancy of the classical KT code, the [MATH] endpoint, and beats both endpoints on every file. An open-source implementation is provided.
tldr: The paper introduces an optimally weighted Krichevsky-Trofimov estimator for adaptive coding with mismatched training data, showing that the effective training length is capped by a harmonic law depending on the KL divergence between training and source.
motivation: Adaptive coders often rely on training data that do not match the source being encoded, and deciding how much to trust such data is a key practical design issue.
method: The authors treat the scaling of training counts in a Krichevsky-Trofimov estimator as a design variable and derive the redundancy-minimizing weight as a function of the KL divergence; they also propose three implementable selectors for the unknown divergence.
result: Weighting removes up to a certain fraction of the redundancy of the classical KT code and outperforms both unweighted and no-training endpoints on every file in the Calgary and Canterbury English corpora.
conclusion: Optimal weighting of training data in adaptive coding provides a principled and practical improvement, with an open-source implementation made available.

title: Security And Privacy In Large-Model-Driven Embodied Agents: Attacks, Defenses, And Future Directions
authors: Lele Zheng, Tong Chen, Ke Cheng, Tao Zhang, Xingchi Liu, Ji He, Xutong Mu, Yulong Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-model-driven embodied agents integrate foundation models with perception, reasoning, planning, and physical action, extending conventional model-level risks into embodied closed loops. Existing studies on their security and privacy remain fragmented across different system components and operational stages, making it difficult to understand how risks arise, propagate, and ultimately affect physical behavior or sensitive information. This survey presents a lifecycle-based analysis of security and privacy in large-model-driven embodied agents. We organize existing research into five stages: model construction and supply chain, multimodal input and interaction, semantic reasoning and task planning, action execution and physical feedback, and long-term deployment. Within this lifecycle, we systematically review representative attacks, defenses, and evaluation methods. Our analysis shows that attack entry, consequence realization, and defense intervention often occur at different stages of the embodied closed loop. It further reveals substantial gaps in end-to-end protection, real-world evaluation, and long-term privacy governance. This survey provides a unified perspective for understanding current progress and identifying critical directions for securing large-model-driven embodied agents.
tldr: A lifecycle-based survey of security and privacy risks in large-model-driven embodied agents, cataloging attacks, defenses, and evaluation methods across five operational stages.
motivation: Large-model-driven embodied agents couple foundation models to perception, reasoning, planning, and physical action, extending model-level risks into embodied closed loops, yet existing security and privacy research remains fragmented across system components and stages.
method: The survey organizes prior work into five lifecycle stages—model construction and supply chain, multimodal input and interaction, semantic reasoning and task planning, action execution and physical feedback, and long-term deployment—reviewing representative attacks, defenses, and evaluation methods at each stage.
result: The analysis shows that attack entry, consequence realization, and defense intervention typically occur at different stages of the embodied closed loop, exposing major gaps in end-to-end protection, real-world evaluation, and long-term privacy governance.
conclusion: The paper offers a unified perspective on securing large-model-driven embodied agents and identifies critical open directions, but remains entirely within AI/robotics security and outside quantum information science.

title: Infectious Behaviour: Simulating The Effects Of Communication And Social Influence On Pathogen Transmission In Crowds
authors: Sophia Johanna Wagner, Anne Templeton, Gerta K\"oster
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public health measures at mass gatherings work only if people follow them, and adherence depends both on how instructions are communicated and what others do. We link these behavioural factors to pathogen transmission in a local-scale, agent-based exposure model combining pedestrian dynamics with airborne transmission. Rather than fitting a parametric behavioural model, agents draw their adherence at run time from survey respondents (2,170 attendees of UK sports and music events) who reported the same context: we vary stewards' communication effectiveness and adherence of role models, as well as agents' shared social identity with each, assuming that strong shared social identity increases their influence. In a ticket-checkpoint queue of 101 agents, effective communication combined with strong shared social identity with stewards reduces the number of highly exposed agents by 82\% for mask wearing. In contrast, strong shared social identity with non-adhering role models gives almost nine times as many highly exposed agents as with adhering role models. Physical distancing was not monotonically beneficial, because adherence changes how agents move: an infectious agent that kept distance moved along the edge of the queue, leading to similar results across conditions. Our pipeline transfers to any survey that includes behavioural measures and contextual variables.
tldr: An agent-based model links communication effectiveness and social influence to pathogen transmission in crowds, showing that strong shared social identity with stewards increases adherence and reduces exposure.
motivation: Public health measures at mass gatherings depend on adherence, which is influenced by how instructions are communicated and by the behavior of others, yet these behavioral factors are rarely integrated into transmission models.
method: The authors combine pedestrian dynamics with an airborne transmission model, drawing agent adherence from survey data of 2,170 UK event attendees and varying communication effectiveness and role-model adherence under different shared social identity assumptions.
result: Effective communication with strong shared social identity with stewards reduced highly exposed agents by 82% for mask wearing, whereas strong shared identity with non-adhering role models produced nearly nine times more highly exposed agents; physical distancing was not monotonically beneficial.
conclusion: Behavioral factors and social identity critically shape pathogen transmission in crowds, and the modular pipeline can be adapted to other surveys with behavioral and contextual measures.

title: Sharp Effective Equidistribution Of Closed Geodesics In Compact Hyperbolic Surfaces
authors: Junehyuk Jung, Insung Park, Peter Zenz
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a sharp effective equidistribution theorem for closed geodesics on a compact hyperbolic surface. This is achieved by carefully analyzing the Selberg trace formula twisted by a Maass eigenfunction, which we refer to as Zelditch's trace formula, following Zelditch's observation that the geometric side can be expressed as a sum of period integrals of eigenfunctions on closed geodesics. The main technical input is a sharp upper bound for the matrix coefficients [MATH] uniformly in [MATH] and [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are the eigenparameters corresponding to Maass forms [MATH] and [MATH] on [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves a sharp effective equidistribution theorem for closed geodesics on compact hyperbolic surfaces using a twisted Selberg trace formula and bounds on matrix coefficients.
motivation: Effective equidistribution of closed geodesics is a central problem in homogeneous dynamics and analytic number theory, with connections to Selberg trace formula and Maass forms.
method: The authors analyze Zelditch's trace formula, expressing the geometric side via period integrals of eigenfunctions, and prove sharp uniform upper bounds for matrix coefficients in terms of the Maass form eigenparameters.
result: They obtain a sharp effective equidistribution theorem for closed geodesics, with quantitative control depending on the spectral parameters.
conclusion: This advances the quantitative theory of geodesic equidistribution and the analytic theory of automorphic forms, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Relative Primal--Dual Gap Certificates For Operator-Composite Trust-Region Methods
authors: Harbir Antil
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study trust-region minimization of a smooth, possibly nonconvex functional plus a convex functional composed with a bounded linear operator. A relative primal--dual gap condition controls both the error in an approximate proximal-gradient step and its linear-model decrease. Together with a computable absolute stationarity test, it yields a finite Cauchy search, convergence of the proximal stationarity measure to zero, and an [MATH] bound on outer trials. The outer analysis allows the linear operator to take values in a Banach space and does not require dual attainment. When the operator takes values in a Hilbert space and the regularizer is finite and Lipschitz, the dual proximal-gradient method produces finite gaps tending to zero, provided the required proximal maps and functional values can be evaluated. We prove [MATH] gap bounds for both recovered and averaged primal candidates and give a sharper bound on the primal error for exactly recovered points. A semilinear elliptic control problem with unsmoothed total-variation regularization and an [MATH] control cost illustrates the method in the full [MATH] metric. Across five meshes, outer and state Newton counts remain constant, while interior-point iteration counts vary mildly.
tldr: The paper develops relative primal-dual gap certificates for operator-composite trust-region methods in nonconvex optimization.
motivation: It aims to solve trust-region minimization of a smooth nonconvex term plus a convex regularizer composed with a bounded linear operator, with applications to semilinear elliptic control problems.
method: The analysis uses a relative primal-dual gap condition to control proximal-gradient step error and model decrease, combined with absolute stationarity tests and dual proximal-gradient methods in Banach and Hilbert spaces.
result: It proves finite Cauchy search, convergence of the proximal stationarity measure, gap bounds for recovered and averaged primal candidates, and demonstrates mesh-independent outer and Newton counts on a semilinear elliptic control problem.
conclusion: The proposed certificates provide a rigorous convergence framework for operator-composite trust-region methods, though the work is outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: G\"odel's And Scott's Variants Of The Ontological Argument In Lean 4
authors: Christoph Benzm\"uller
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a complete, structure-preserving port to Lean 4 of the Isabelle/HOL dataset accompanying Benzm\"uller and Scott's study of G\"odel's modal ontological argument and Scott's variant of it. The port comprises 30 Lean 4 modules, one per Isabelle/HOL theory, retaining the section structure, the declaration order and the name of every axiom, definition, lemma and theorem; a comparison tool certifies all 548 statements identical. Everything the Isabelle/HOL development proves is proved again, including the inconsistency of G\"odel's 1970 axioms, the repaired G\"odel variants, Scott's variant, modal collapse, monotheism and the ultrafilter property of the positive properties; five statements the original leaves unreplayed after an automated prover had found a proof, one of which it then postulates, are proved as well. The 45 remaining unproved statements are exactly those the original refutes by nitpick (35) or leaves open (10); they are anonymous sorrys on which nothing depends. Two features of Lean 4 shape the result. It has neither a sledgehammer nor a model finder, so the one-line automated proofs become explicit proof terms and the 72 nitpick invocations are recorded as documentation. And #print axioms reports the postulates each proof consumes, giving for every result an upper bound on the modal logic it requires: Scott's necessary-existence theorem and modal collapse need only symmetry of the accessibility relation (logic KB); the essence and monotheism lemmas and the possible existence of a God-like being need no frame condition (the latter with the one exception the original records, the mixed-quantifier setting); and the inconsistency of G\"odel's 1970 axioms needs none either. The development depends on no library beyond Lean 4's core; sources, comparison tools and two Isabelle cross-check sessions are included as ancillary files.
tldr: The paper presents a complete, structure-preserving port of Gödel's and Scott's modal ontological argument from Isabelle/HOL to Lean 4, verifying 548 statements and proving additional results.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a faithful Lean 4 reconstruction of an existing Isabelle/HOL formalization of Gödel's and Scott's ontological argument, enabling independent verification and analysis of the modal logic dependencies.
method: They port 30 Isabelle/HOL theories into 30 Lean 4 modules, preserving section structure, declaration order, and names, and use a comparison tool to certify statement identity; automated Isabelle proofs are replaced by explicit Lean proof terms, with #print axioms used to determine required modal frame conditions.
result: The formalization reproduces all previously proved results, adds proofs for five statements left unreplayed, and shows that Scott's necessary-existence theorem and modal collapse need only symmetry (KB), while the essence and monotheism lemmas need no frame condition and Gödel's 1970 axioms are inconsistent.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the feasibility of structure-preserving formalization transfer between proof assistants and provides a detailed account of the modal logic strength needed for each theorem in the ontological argument.

title: Topological Signatures Of Cyber-Attack Classes In Natural Visibility Graph Representations Of Network Traffic
authors: Ilker Turker Ali Melih Kanca
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Natural Visibility Graph (NVG)-based representations provide a promising approach for capturing structural patterns in sequential network traffic. However, whether different cyber-attack classes exhibit distinctive topological signatures in such representations remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the discriminative and structural characteristics of NVG-based network traffic representations using the CSE-CIC-IDS2018 dataset. Seventy-six numerical traffic features were independently transformed into NVGs within overlapping frames of 40 observations, and ten graph-theoretic metrics were extracted from each graph, resulting in 760 topological descriptors per frame. The discriminative capability of these representations was evaluated using a multi-branch convolutional neural network (CNN) with stratified five-fold cross-validation. The model achieved an average accuracy of 96.20% and a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.9566. To characterize class-specific topological differences, Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U tests were combined with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction and effect-size measures. Of the 10,640 attack-versus-benign comparisons, 7,777 (73.1%) remained statistically significant after FDR correction, with 4,844 exhibiting large Cliff's delta effects. The strongest global differences were predominantly associated with backward-traffic and packet-length-related features combined with connectivity, clustering, and centrality measures. These findings indicate that NVG-derived representations can provide strong discriminative capability while revealing class-dependent topological patterns associated with different cyber-attack classes.
tldr: The paper uses natural visibility graphs of network traffic features to classify cyber-attack types, finding strong discriminative topological signatures.
motivation: Detecting and distinguishing cyber-attack classes from sequential network traffic is important, but whether graph-based representations reveal class-specific structural patterns is not well understood.
method: Seventy-six traffic features from the CSE-CIC-IDS2018 dataset were converted into natural visibility graphs over overlapping 40-observation frames, and ten graph-theoretic metrics per graph were fed to a multi-branch CNN with stratified five-fold cross-validation.
result: The model achieved 96.20% average accuracy and MCC 0.9566, with 73.1% of attack-vs-benign graph metric comparisons remaining significant after FDR correction and many large effect sizes.
conclusion: NVG-based representations offer strong cyber-attack discrimination and expose class-dependent topological patterns, suggesting utility for network intrusion detection.

title: Mdrc: A Deployable State-Recovery Defense For Traffic Signal Control Under Sensor Corruption
authors: Mingyuan Li, Chunyu Liu, Xiao Liu, Yanna Jiang, Guangsheng Yu, Xu Wang, Wei Ni, Ren Ping Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traffic Signal Control (TSC) is a safety-critical cyber-physical system that relies on real-time sensing. Corrupted observations caused by adversarial perturbations or sensor failures can propagate from the sensing layer into the controller and degrade traffic efficiency. Existing robust Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based TSC methods often suffer from limited cross-city generalization, high inference latency, and weak recovery under partial observability. We present MDRC (Meta-Diffusion-based framework for Resilient traffic signal Control against adversarial attacks and sensor failures), a post-detection state-recovery defense inserted between sensing and control. MDRC reconstructs trustworthy traffic states before they are consumed by the controller. It combines Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models (DDIM) for efficient state recovery with Reptile meta-learning for a transferable initialization across cities. We provide an optimization-based view of the DDIM recovery dynamics and establish a recovery-error bound that separates score approximation, numerical discretization, and initialization mismatch. Across seven real-world-derived CityFlow benchmarks, MDRC reduces Average Travel Time by 6.77% under stochastic and policy-aware attacks and by 12.75% under structured sensor loss, while improving state-recovery fidelity. We further evaluate 3,600 seconds of real roadside measurements with 50% of detector channels disabled and integrate MDRC into a hardware-in-the-loop traffic-signal stack. Over a 9.16-hour run with 32,389 sensing/control cycles, the system achieves 99.79% decision availability, produces no out-of-plan recommendations, and requires approximately 38 ms of component-wise processing per one-second control interval.
tldr: MDRC is a post-detection state-recovery defense for traffic signal control that combines DDIM-based reconstruction with Reptile meta-learning to mitigate sensor corruption and failures.
motivation: Traffic signal control is safety-critical, but corrupted observations from adversarial attacks or sensor failures can propagate into controllers and degrade performance. Existing robust RL-based TSC methods struggle with cross-city generalization, inference latency, and recovery under partial observability.
method: MDRC inserts a state-recovery module between sensing and control, using Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models for efficient traffic-state reconstruction and Reptile meta-learning for transferable initialization across cities. The authors also provide an optimization-based analysis of DDIM recovery dynamics and a recovery-error bound.
result: Across seven CityFlow benchmarks, MDRC reduces Average Travel Time by 6.77% under stochastic and policy-aware attacks and by 12.75% under structured sensor loss, while improving state-recovery fidelity. A hardware-in-the-loop deployment over 9.16 hours achieved 99.79% decision availability with about 38 ms processing per control interval.
conclusion: MDRC offers a deployable defense for traffic signal control under sensor corruption, improving robustness and recovery in simulation and real-world roadside measurements, though it is outside the scope of quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Structural Resilience Of Space-Time Wave Packets To Volumetric Scattering
authors: Kefu Mu, Hsiao-Chih Huang, Chen-Ting Liao, Hui Min Leung
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical space-time wave packets (STWPs) can be engineered to sustain tight transverse confinement over long distances. However, whether the requisite precise spatiotemporal correlations underlying this behavior survive volumetric scattering remains unclear. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that STWP light sheets with transverse thicknesses of 11 and 22 microns largely retain their prescribed spatiotemporal structure after transmission through 10 mm thick scattering phantoms (scattering coefficient = 0.84 per mm). Moreover, compared with size-matched Gaussian beams, STWPs exhibit greater preservation of their initial spectral intensity distribution across the prescribed space-time domain following scattering. Additionally, the transmitted STWPs remain tightly confined and preserve on-axis intensity decay rates similar to those of their unscattered counterparts. As the scattering conditions span biologically relevant regimes, the structural and propagation resilience of STWPs to scattering highlights their potential for extended-depth 3D biomedical microscopy.
tldr: Optical space-time wave packets retain their spatiotemporal structure after passing through thick volumetric scattering phantoms, outperforming Gaussian beams and suggesting use in deep-tissue microscopy.
motivation: It is unclear whether the precise spatiotemporal correlations defining space-time wave packets survive volumetric scattering, which is important for potential biomedical imaging applications.
method: The authors experimentally transmit STWP light sheets with 11 and 22 micron transverse thickness through 10 mm thick scattering phantoms (scattering coefficient 0.84/mm) and compare their spectral and spatial properties to size-matched Gaussian beams.
result: STWPs largely preserve their prescribed spatiotemporal structure, maintain tighter confinement, and exhibit on-axis intensity decay rates similar to unscattered counterparts, while better preserving spectral intensity distributions than Gaussian beams.
conclusion: The structural resilience of STWPs under biologically relevant scattering conditions highlights their potential for extended-depth 3D biomedical microscopy.

title: The Rademacher Quotient Of $l^1$ Embeds Into $l^1$ And Its Weak Calkin Algebra Is Uniformly Incompressible
authors: Amir Bahman Nasseri
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be the closed linear span of the Rademacher functions in [MATH]. We prove that [MATH] embeds isomorphically into [MATH], answering affirmatively a question of Gonz\'alez and Mart\'inez-Abej\'on \cite[p.~140]{GM97}. We then use this embedding to show that the weak Calkin algebra of the quotient is uniformly incompressible. \end{abstract.
tldr: The closed linear span of the Rademacher functions is shown to embed isomorphically into l^1, and this embedding yields uniform incompressibility of the weak Calkin algebra of the quotient.
motivation: The paper answers affirmatively an open question of González and Martínez-Abejón concerning whether the Rademacher quotient of l^1 embeds into l^1.
method: Banach space and operator algebra techniques are used to construct an isomorphic embedding of the Rademacher span into l^1, which is then applied to analyze the weak Calkin algebra of the resulting quotient.
result: The Rademacher span embeds isomorphically into l^1, and consequently the weak Calkin algebra of the quotient is shown to be uniformly incompressible.
conclusion: The work resolves a known open problem in Banach space theory and connects the embedding result to structural properties of Calkin-type algebras.

title: Differentiability Of Lipschitz Curves In $p$-Banach Spaces
authors: Fernando Albiac, Jos\'e L. Ansorena, Pietro Wald
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The problem of differentiating Lipschitz curves in Banach spaces goes back to Tamarkin in the early 1930s and is one of the origins of the Radon--Nikod\'ym property in classical Banach space theory. In this article we characterize those quasi-Banach spaces [MATH] for which every Lipschitz curve [MATH] admits a point of differentiability and prove that this property holds if and only if [MATH] is isomorphic to a Banach space with the Radon--Nikod\'ym property, thus substantiating a conjecture of Kalton, communicated personally to the first-named author in 2008. Equivalently, every nonlocally convex quasi-Banach space admits a nowhere differentiable Lipschitz curve. Our result is obtained from a quantitative characterization of local convexity in terms of the infinitesimal oscillation of Lipschitz curves. Motivated by this obstruction, we then investigate positive differentiability phenomena in [MATH], [MATH], and identify natural decoupled-coordinate constructions for which Lipschitz regularity nevertheless implies almost-everywhere differentiability. We also contrast this behavior with metric differentiability for the natural metric and the quasi-metric on [MATH].
tldr: The paper characterizes quasi-Banach spaces in which every Lipschitz curve is differentiable somewhere, proving this holds exactly when the space is isomorphic to a Banach space with the Radon–Nikodym property.
motivation: Differentiability of Lipschitz curves dates to Tamarkin (1930s) and is an origin of the Radon–Nikodym property in classical Banach space theory; Kalton conjectured a characterization for quasi-Banach spaces in 2008.
method: The authors establish a quantitative characterization of local convexity via the infinitesimal oscillation of Lipschitz curves, and then analyze decoupled-coordinate constructions in specific non-locally convex spaces.
result: They confirm Kalton's conjecture: every Lipschitz curve admits a point of differentiability iff the space is isomorphic to a Banach space with the Radon–Nikodym property; equivalently every nonlocally convex quasi-Banach space admits a nowhere-differentiable Lipschitz curve.
conclusion: Beyond the negative result, they identify natural settings where Lipschitz regularity still yields almost-everywhere differentiability, and contrast metric differentiability for the natural metric and quasi-metric.

title: Change Detection With Conformal Martingales: New Optimal Constructions, And Suboptimality Of Existing Methods
authors: Aaditya Ramdas Swapnaneel Bhattacharyya
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study distribution-free sequential changepoint detection for independent observations with unknown and unrestricted pre- and post-change laws. We build on the conformal test martingales and associated e-detectors of Vovk(2021), which control the probability of false alarm (PFA) and the average run length (ARL) respectively. The majority of these works focus on validity, with statistical efficiency usually left for simulations. We develop a comprehensive theory of how conformal p-values behave under non-exchangeable data with a changepoint at an unknown time [MATH]. We use this to analyze the post-change growth and resulting detection delay of conformal martingale methods, and prove that the standard existing methods are suboptimal for PFA and ARL control, and can lead to delays that are [MATH] and [MATH] respectively. We propose different conformal e-processes and e-detectors that are provably minimax optimal, with delays [MATH] and [MATH] respectively, and have much shorter delays in simulations.
tldr: The paper develops a theory of conformal test martingales for distribution-free sequential changepoint detection, proving existing methods suboptimal and constructing minimax-optimal conformal e-processes and e-detectors.
motivation: Conformal martingale approaches to changepoint detection have been validated for false-alarm control but their statistical efficiency and detection delay have largely been unexplored theoretically, leaving room to characterize and improve upon standard methods.
method: The authors analyze the behavior of conformal p-values under non-exchangeable data with an unknown changepoint time, deriving post-change growth rates of conformal martingales and then proposing new conformal e-processes and e-detectors designed to achieve provable minimax-optimal delay.
result: They prove that standard existing conformal martingale methods for PFA and ARL control are suboptimal, yielding delays of certain orders, whereas the proposed e-processes and e-detectors achieve minimax-optimal delays and shorter delays in simulations.
conclusion: The work provides both a theoretical characterization of conformal change-detection performance and improved, provably optimal constructions, showing the suboptimality of prior approaches and offering better practical detection delays.

title: Stability Analysis Of Decentralized Adaptive Control Of Laterally Coupled Multi-Loop Thermosyphon System With Unknown System Parameters
authors: Yan Wu Novel Kumar Dey
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A high dimensional bi-directionally coupled [MATH]-loop thermosyphon system in a tandem is modeled by [MATH] Lorenz type of differential equations. The fluid flow in each loop is driven by the heat source (Rayleigh numbers) as well as the moment and heat exchanges between the adjacent loops. The flow becomes chaotic when the Rayleigh numbers are large. A decentralized controller design via proportional local state feedback is employed to stabilize the chaotic flows in each loop. As a result of the stability analysis, we show that there exist lower bounds on the controller gains that guarantee global stability of the system. Under the scenario of unknown parameters, we augment the original system with additional dynamic equations of the feedback gains to adaptively determine the feasible gains that stabilize the system. The analysis also sheds insight on the role of thermal coupling in the stability of the control system, which allows us to extend the results to negative [MATH]-state coupling coefficient as well as a class of nonlinear [MATH]-state coupling functions. Numerical simulations further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed controller design.
tldr: This paper studies decentralized adaptive control for stabilizing chaotic flows in a high-dimensional laterally coupled multi-loop thermosyphon system modeled by Lorenz-type equations.
motivation: The authors aim to control chaotic fluid flow in coupled thermosyphon loops and determine controller gains when system parameters are unknown.
method: A proportional local state feedback controller is designed, with lower bounds on gains for global stability, and the system is augmented with adaptive gain dynamics to handle unknown parameters.
result: The analysis shows that feasible controller gains exist that guarantee global stability, and numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive decentralized controller.
conclusion: The results provide stability conditions for controlling coupled thermosyphon systems and extend to negative coupling coefficients and a class of nonlinear coupling functions.

title: From Variational Optimization To Flow-Based Transport: Posterior-Geometry Regularization For Ill-Conditioned Data Assimilation
authors: Siming Liang, Feng Bao, Hristo G. Chipilski, Peter Jan van Leeuwen, Guannan Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variational data assimilation computes a Bayesian update through optimization on a fixed posterior geometry, whose conditioning is determined by the prior covariance and the observation operator. In strongly anisotropic, weakly observed, or highly informative regimes, this geometry can become severely ill conditioned, leading to substantial sensitivity to solver design and preconditioning. This work investigates an alternative computational route based on flow-based transport, using the ensemble score filter as a training-free realization. Rather than repeatedly optimizing over the full posterior geometry, the flow-based update transports the predictive distribution through a sequence of intermediate distributions whose covariance and curvature are progressively regularized before reaching the target posterior. In the linear-Gaussian setting, we characterize this mechanism through the evolution of the diffused posterior covariance and the associated time-dependent curvature, revealing a continuation from a near-isotropic reference geometry to the ill-conditioned posterior geometry targeted by variational assimilation. Numerical stress tests show that this geometric regularization makes the flow-based method substantially less sensitive to severe ill-conditioning than the variational method, while a heterogeneous [MATH]-dimensional Lorenz-96 benchmark demonstrates improved robustness and lower delivered computational cost. These results identify posterior-geometry regularization as a key mechanism distinguishing transport-based from optimization-based data assimilation.
tldr: The paper compares variational data assimilation with a flow-based transport method, showing that posterior-geometry regularization makes the flow-based approach more robust to ill-conditioning.
motivation: Variational data assimilation can become severely ill-conditioned in anisotropic, weakly observed, or highly informative regimes, causing sensitivity to solver design and preconditioning.
method: The authors use the ensemble score filter as a training-free flow-based transport realization and analyze the evolution of the diffused posterior covariance and time-dependent curvature in the linear-Gaussian setting.
result: Numerical stress tests and a Lorenz-96 benchmark show the flow-based method is substantially less sensitive to ill-conditioning and has lower delivered computational cost than the variational method.
conclusion: Posterior-geometry regularization is identified as a key mechanism distinguishing transport-based from optimization-based data assimilation.

title: A Deformation Approach To Axially Symmetric Kernels On The Sphere: Harmonic Coupling And Regularity
authors: Fabian Stallbauer Janin J\"ager
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct axially symmetric kernels on the sphere. We start by taking an isotropic kernel and transform it into an axially symmetric kernel via a specific deformation. For a general deformation, an explicit spherical-harmonic representation is not necessarily available. For our deformation, we can obtain such a representation of the deformed kernel in terms of the expansion coefficients of the original isotropic kernel. We derive this representation by explicitly describing the effect of the deformation on the spherical harmonic basis. From this, an explicit finite sum formula for the coupling coefficients is deduced and we show that, for each fixed input mode, the coefficients decay geometrically at a rate controlled by our deformation parameter. We further note that if the native space of the isotropic kernel is norm equivalent to a Sobolev-space, then the deformed kernel has the same native space with an equivalent norm. In our numerical experiments, we show that our deformation can improve prediction when the underlying random field has an axially symmetric covariance.
tldr: The paper constructs axially symmetric kernels on the sphere by deforming isotropic kernels, deriving explicit spherical-harmonic representations, geometrically decaying coupling coefficients, and native-space (Sobolev) equivalence results, with numerical experiments for axially symmetric random-field covariances.
motivation: Many applications involving data on the sphere require kernels that are anisotropic yet tractable, and general deformations of isotropic kernels usually lack explicit spherical-harmonic expansions.
method: An isotropic positive-definite kernel is transformed via a specific deformation; the action of the deformation on the spherical-harmonic basis is described explicitly to obtain a finite-sum formula for harmonic coupling coefficients, and native-space norm equivalence to a Sobolev space is analyzed.
result: Explicit spherical-harmonic coefficients of the deformed kernel are obtained from those of the isotropic kernel, with coupling coefficients decaying geometrically at a rate set by the deformation parameter, and the deformed kernel preserves the native space (with equivalent norm) when the isotropic kernel does so.
conclusion: The deformation provides a practical, theoretically grounded route to axially symmetric kernels on the sphere and can improve prediction when the underlying random field has axially symmetric covariance.

title: Component-wise Accurate Fixed Point Iterations For Computing The Square Root Of A Singular M-matrix
authors: Dario Andrea Bini, Bruno Iannazzo, Beatrice Meini, Jie Meng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze two fixed-point iterations for computing the principal square root of an M-matrix [MATH]. Although these iterations, with customary initialization, converge sublinearly when [MATH] is a singular M-matrix, we show that, under suitable mild conditions on the initial approximation, the convergence is linear. Moreover, we provide component-wise accurate versions of these iterations, which allow us to approximate the principal square root with a component-wise relative error uniformly bounded by a small multiple of the machine precision. Numerical experiments demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms for certain classes of problems are presented.
tldr: The paper develops component-wise accurate fixed-point iterations for computing the principal square root of a singular M-matrix, achieving relative error near machine precision.
motivation: Computing matrix square roots of singular M-matrices is difficult because standard fixed-point iterations converge only sublinearly under customary initialization.
method: The authors analyze two fixed-point iterations and show that with suitable mild conditions on the initial approximation, convergence becomes linear; they then construct component-wise accurate variants.
result: The proposed algorithms approximate the principal square root with component-wise relative error uniformly bounded by a small multiple of machine precision, validated by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The component-wise accurate iterations extend the applicability and accuracy of matrix square root computations for singular M-matrices, with demonstrated effectiveness on certain problem classes.

title: When Clients Are Orchestrated: Strategic Gradient Manipulation To Defeat Federated Learning Servers With Efficient Defense
authors: Mohamed Shaaban, Ahmed Abdelnaby, Mohamed Elmahallawy
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated Learning enables decentralized model training by exchanging model updates--rather than raw data--with a central parameter server (PS). While most of the existing defenses primarily assume static or independently acting adversaries, we reveal a new class of dynamically adaptive attacks that systematically bypass such protections. We propose Fed-ADR, a holistic attack framework in which a malicious orchestrator server (OS) dynamically coordinates a heterogeneous set of adversarial clients, including both targeted and untargeted attackers. Through real-time coordination by the OS, malicious clients strategically adapt their gradient updates to evade defenses deployed by the PS, while either severely degrading global model performance or steering training toward adversarial objectives.To mitigate this threat, we offer a detection mechanism that estimates each client's true gradient from historical updates, enabling real-time detection of coordinated malicious behavior without additional overhead. We further introduce an in-situ recovery mechanism that restores global model performance without restarting training, preserving convergence and minimizing recovery time. Comprehensive experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 benchmark datasets demonstrate that Fed-ADR's attack scheme can reduce global accuracy from over 90% to below 10%, bypassing several state-of-the-art defenses. When our detection and recovery modules are employed, they identify malicious clients and restore accuracy to over 90% within a few rounds, at a substantially lower cost than retraining from scratch--achieving a reduction of at least 20x in computational overhead.
tldr: The paper proposes Fed-ADR, a coordinated attack framework in federated learning where a malicious orchestrator server dynamically manipulates adversarial clients' gradient updates to bypass defenses, along with detection and recovery mechanisms.
motivation: Most existing federated learning defenses assume static or independently acting adversaries, leaving them vulnerable to dynamically adaptive and coordinated attacks.
method: Fed-ADR uses a malicious orchestrator server to coordinate heterogeneous targeted and untargeted adversarial clients in real time, while a detection mechanism estimates each client's true gradient from historical updates and an in-situ recovery mechanism restores model performance without restarting training.
result: Experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 show that Fed-ADR reduces global accuracy from over 90% to below 10%, bypassing several state-of-the-art defenses, and the proposed detection and recovery modules restore accuracy to over 90% within a few rounds with at least 20x lower computational overhead than retraining from scratch.
conclusion: The work reveals a new class of adaptive coordinated attacks in federated learning and offers efficient detection and recovery defenses, but it is entirely classical and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ccr: Towards A Common, Quality-Gated Cacao Integrations Registry For European Cybersecurity Automation
authors: Mateusz Zych, Vasileios Mavroeidis, Gudmund Grov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standardised, machine-readable cybersecurity playbooks provide a basis for portable, shareable, and reusable incident-response logic. OASIS CACAO provides a vendor-neutral representation for such playbooks, but not the product-specific integration artefacts needed to invoke external products and services. We introduce the Common CACAO Registry (CCR), an open, provenance-aware registry of CACAO HTTP-API connector envelopes. Each envelope captures an API operation's command, inputs, target, authentication-related information, provenance, validation evidence, and maturity metadata. CCR is , with acceptance requiring both CACAO v2 schema validity and a mean back-validation score of at least 0.8 against the source OpenAPI operation, while a six-level maturity model records progressively stronger evidence and distinguishes gate acceptance from operational readiness. To seed CCR, we develop a hybrid OpenAPI-to-CACAO pipeline. Deterministic code extracts source-derived interface facts, generates identifiers, wires cross-references, and validates structure, while a constrained LLM provides bounded semantic enrichment, including action naming, authentication interpretation, and CACAO activity annotation. Evaluation across eight security APIs yields 713 CACAO-schema-valid envelopes with a mean back-validation score of 91.5\%, of which 675 produce well-formed, dispatchable HTTP requests in a local harness. Comparison with a deterministic rule-based baseline shows that mechanical API structure is preserved more reliably through rule-based translation, while the LLM contributes bounded semantic enrichment, most notably CACAO activity annotation. Together, these results support CCR as reusable integration infrastructure for CACAO action steps and as an initial foundation for a broader common European registry.
tldr: The paper introduces the Common CACAO Registry (CCR), an open, provenance-aware registry of CACAO HTTP-API connector envelopes for European cybersecurity automation, seeded via a hybrid OpenAPI-to-CACAO pipeline.
motivation: Standardized, machine-readable cybersecurity playbooks such as OASIS CACAO lack product-specific integration artefacts needed to invoke external products and services. CCR aims to fill this gap with reusable, validated integration infrastructure.
method: A hybrid pipeline combines deterministic code extraction of OpenAPI facts with constrained LLM-based semantic enrichment to generate CACAO connector envelopes. Validation requires CACAO v2 schema validity and a mean back-validation score of at least 0.8 against the source OpenAPI operation, with a six-level maturity model.
result: Evaluation across eight security APIs yields 713 CACAO-schema-valid envelopes with a mean back-validation score of 91.5%, of which 675 produce well-formed dispatchable HTTP requests. Rule-based translation preserves mechanical API structure more reliably, while the LLM contributes bounded semantic enrichment, especially CACAO activity annotation.
conclusion: CCR supports reusable integration infrastructure for CACAO action steps and serves as an initial foundation for a broader common European registry, though it is outside quantum information science.

title: Agent Name Collision Attacks In Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Adithyan Arun Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent hosts turn remote Agent Cards into local agents, tools, workflow targets, and broker routes. A2A defines the card's name as human-readable metadata, not as a stable identity, and specifies no collision semantics. The security failure begins when a host nevertheless uses that remote name as a local routing identifier. We traced registration through dispatch and ran isolated regression tests at seven pinned open-source revisions. Six client-style integrations selected an attacker-controlled peer's client or loopback endpoint for a request addressed to a trusted peer's name. A seventh, brokered implementation collapsed both peers onto one name-derived route; queue and access-control state determine whether the result is interception or denial. The common result is wrong-peer dispatch, not universal privilege inheritance. Synthetic credential and tool tests found no A-specific credential transfer in the tested client bindings and no direct transfer of A-owned tools. The broker path forwards a caller-configuration object; delegated identity or tokens reach B only if present and B can consume the route. Two other paths expose a later, model-mediated decision rather than direct execution authority. The necessary conditions assign different responsibilities to the protocol, implementations, and deployments. Hosts should route by an origin-bound stable identity, keep names presentational, and reject ambiguous aliases. The evidence establishes a recurring implementation vulnerability class, not a universal A2A protocol exploit or a count of vulnerable deployments.
tldr: The paper identifies an implementation vulnerability class in multi-agent A2A systems where remote Agent Card names are used as local routing identifiers, enabling wrong-peer dispatch.
motivation: A2A defines an Agent Card's name as human-readable metadata rather than a stable identity and specifies no collision semantics, so hosts that nevertheless route by that remote name may select the wrong peer.
method: The authors traced registration-to-dispatch paths and ran isolated regression tests at seven pinned open-source revisions, including synthetic credential and tool tests.
result: Six client-style integrations dispatched requests addressed to a trusted peer to an attacker-controlled client or loopback endpoint, and a seventh brokered implementation collapsed both peers onto one name-derived route, yielding interception or denial without universal privilege inheritance.
conclusion: The findings establish a recurring implementation vulnerability class rather than a universal A2A protocol exploit, and recommend routing by origin-bound stable identity while keeping names presentational and rejecting ambiguous aliases.

title: The Hidden Life Of Signals: Time-domain Inferences And Other Privacy Attacks On Everyday Devices
authors: Larry Hernandez
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In privacy research on radiofrequency-based protocols, the dominant focus has remained on Bluetooth, WiFi, and Zigbee, while a broader and arguably more consequential attack surface has gone largely unnoticed: the privacy risks created by the composition of everyday wireless protocols. Widely deployed systems such as KeeLoq remotes, vehicle TPMS sensors, and other sub-GHz devices continuously emit metadata and timing structure that, when analyzed jointly rather than in isolation, enable powerful behavioral inference. This work-in-progress paper argues that privacy leakage in these environments is not merely a property of individual protocols, but an emergent property of their interaction, correlation, and composition across devices, spaces, and routines. The resulting attack surface arises both from protocol metadata that directly degrades privacy and from the latent relationships between devices and the ways users move among and interact with them over time. We present preliminary evidence that these composed signals expose underappreciated opportunities for inference and tracking, and we outline a research agenda for characterizing and mitigating this broader class of privacy failures.
tldr: A work-in-progress paper arguing that privacy leakage in everyday sub-GHz wireless devices (KeeLoq remotes, TPMS sensors) is an emergent property of protocol composition rather than of individual protocols.
motivation: Privacy research has focused narrowly on Bluetooth, WiFi, and Zigbee, leaving a broader and potentially more consequential attack surface from composed everyday wireless protocols largely unexplored.
method: The authors analyze metadata and timing structure emitted jointly across multiple sub-GHz devices and user routines, presenting preliminary evidence of inference and tracking opportunities and outlining a research agenda.
result: Initial evidence suggests that correlated, cross-device signal analysis exposes behavioral inference and tracking capabilities not visible when protocols are studied in isolation.
conclusion: The paper calls for a research agenda to characterize and mitigate this emergent class of compositional privacy failures in everyday wireless environments.

title: MixGuard: Towards Detecting And Understanding Mixer Laundering On Ethereum
authors: Qishuang Fu, Hang Zheng, Xihan Xiong, Joseph K. Liu, Yixin Liu, Shirui Pan, Qin Wang, Weiqing Wang, Zhipeng Wang, Tsz Hon Yuen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixers protect privacy by concealing deposit--withdrawal links, but are also abused to launder illicit funds. Existing anti-money laundering studies do not specifically target mixer laundering, while mixer research focuses on deanonymization rather than identifying laundering-related transactions. Public reports remain fragmented, leaving no public case-level dataset for systematic measurement and detection. To fill this void, this paper presents the first comprehensive study of mixer laundering on Ethereum. We first construct , the first public case-level dataset of mixer laundering. It covers 27 cases involving Tornado Cash and Railgun from 2020 to 2025 and labels 9,300 laundering-related transactions with case identities and observable upstream and downstream fund flows, including deposits totaling approximately \$1.1 billion. By comparing these transactions with background mixer usage, we identify five common strategies, showing that laundering evidence spans complementary behavioral and fund-flow contexts, while same-case activity is locally tight but weakly connected across bursts. Our analysis further reveals coverage gaps in mixer-side risk screening and representative deanonymization heuristics. Guided by these findings, we develop , which combines tri-view representation learning with two-stage grouping for transaction-level detection and case-aware grouping. Under strict case-level holdout evaluation, outperforms representative baselines, achieving 97.89\% detection precision and 98.73\% group purity, while its top ten groups cover 95.09\% of each case's transactions on average.
tldr: MixGuard is the first comprehensive study and detection framework for cryptocurrency mixer laundering on Ethereum, built on a new public case-level dataset of Tornado Cash and Railgun transactions.
motivation: Mixers like Tornado Cash and Railgun conceal deposit-withdrawal links and are abused for money laundering, yet existing anti-money-laundering work does not specifically target mixer laundering and no public case-level dataset exists for systematic measurement.
method: The authors construct a case-level dataset of 27 laundering cases (2020-2025) labeling 9,300 transactions, identify five common laundering strategies via comparison with background mixer usage, then develop MixGuard combining tri-view representation learning with two-stage grouping for transaction-level detection and case-aware grouping.
result: Under strict case-level holdout evaluation, MixGuard achieves 97.89% detection precision and 98.73% group purity, with its top ten groups covering 95.09% of each case's transactions on average, outperforming representative baselines.
conclusion: The work exposes coverage gaps in mixer-side risk screening and deanonymization heuristics, and provides both a public dataset and an effective detection framework for blockchain anti-money-laundering.

title: Coherent Multidimensional Spectroscopy At The Few-Cycle Limit: Accounting For The Pump Spectrum
authors: Jacob S. Higgins, Gerrit N. Christenson, James D. Gaynor
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherent multidimensional spectroscopy will benefit greatly from near single-cycle pulses through the spectral breadth of states that can be accessed and the high frequency oscillations that can be resolved. However, the necessary cost of working with such pulses is the spectral structure arising from efficient self-phase modulation, which imparts into the signal and complicates interpretation of the molecular response. In this paper, we develop an in-operando approach to characterize and remove pump spectral features from two-dimensional spectroscopic signals. The pump spectrum is retrieved via an interferometric integrated autocorrelation measurement that runs concurrently with the experiment and thereby inherits the same time and frequency domain properties.
