Experiments support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. Notably, by exploiting the like-score feedback loop, the attack causes the recommendation system to select poisoned posts even when their user-post similarity falls below the retrieval threshold.
tldr: The paper studies multi-stage data poisoning attacks that exploit the like-score feedback loop of similarity-based recommendation systems to steer LLM-based agents' feeds toward adversarial content.
motivation: LLM agents increasingly act autonomously on social media, yet their vulnerability to subtle, recommendation-system-mediated poisoning (rather than direct exposure to malicious content) remains underexplored.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the like-score mechanism in OASIS, characterize conditions under which a chain of poisoned posts can propagate through the feed, and design an algorithm to craft realistic poisoned posts.
result: Experiments confirm the theoretical analysis, showing the attack successfully causes the recommender to surface poisoned posts even when user-post similarity falls below the retrieval threshold.
conclusion: Indirect, feedback-loop-driven poisoning is a viable and stealthier threat to LLM agents on social platforms, highlighting the need for defenses at the recommendation-system level.

title: Understanding Human Perception Of Representation In Citizens' Assemblies: An Empirical Study
authors: Yusuf Hakan Kalayci, Vasilis Varsamis, Nick Gill, Evi Micha
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Citizens' assemblies are deliberative bodies intended to form a microcosm of the population. Organizers rely on quota-based stratification and must decide which attributes define resemblance to the public. Yet meeting every quota can still leave a dimension citizens value unrepresented. We study this attribute-selection problem in general-purpose and climate-focused assemblies through randomized conjoint experiments. We find that demographic attributes matter for perceived representation, but political alignment and context-specific attributes such as climate concern exert a stronger influence. When both are shown in a climate-focused setting, each remains influential, with political alignment having the larger estimated marginal effect. We also examine the omission of a relevant stratification attribute. Panels stratified on demographics, even with political alignment included, match the observed pool's climate-concern distribution no better than uniform random samples. These results suggest that representation on a relevant topic-specific attribute cannot always be recovered through correlated demographic or political quotas, and may therefore require explicit stratification. Finally, we ask whether representation preferences can be learned from the observed profiles. We compare predictive models, from simple, interpretable matching rules to a learned metric and a respondent-conditioned utility model. Both learned models predict choices for respondents excluded from training with substantial accuracy, revealing generalizable structure without fully capturing these judgments. Together, these findings guide attribute selection in citizens' assemblies: designers should consider political and topic-specific dimensions alongside demographics, avoid assuming correlated proxies protect omitted dimensions, and use predictive models to diagnose how profiles shape representation choices.
tldr: An empirical conjoint-experiment study on how citizens perceive representation in citizens' assemblies, examining which stratification attributes (demographic, political, topic-specific) drive perceived resemblance.
motivation: Organizers of citizens' assemblies must choose which attributes define a representative sample, yet meeting demographic quotas can still leave valued dimensions unrepresented; the authors investigate how attribute selection affects perceived representation.
method: Randomized conjoint experiments in general-purpose and climate-focused assembly settings, combined with predictive modeling approaches ranging from interpretable matching rules to a learned metric and a respondent-conditioned utility model.
result: Demographic attributes matter for perceived representation, but political alignment and context-specific attributes such as climate concern exert stronger influence; demographic-stratified panels do not recover the climate-concern distribution better than uniform random samples, and learned models predict out-of-sample respondent choices with substantial accuracy.
conclusion: Designers should consider political and topic-specific dimensions alongside demographics, avoid assuming correlated proxies protect omitted dimensions, and use predictive models to diagnose how profiles shape representation choices.

title: The Complexity Of Interference: When Rely/Guarantee Does Not Work
authors: Nisansala P. Yatapanage
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rely/Guarantee is a well-known verification technique for reasoning about concurrent programs. However, for some algorithms, devising suitable rely and guarantee conditions is challenging, due to the strong interference exhibited in these algorithms. The Ben-Ari concurrent garbage collector is an algorithm where the complex interactions between the components prevent the construction of compositional rely and guarantee conditions. This paper investigates an approach for verifying the Ben-Ari algorithm, which enables reasoning to be performed in a more compositional manner in cases where compositional reasoning would not otherwise be possible. This is accomplished by reasoning that a given property holds for all instances of a particular variable and then instantiating the variable to the local variable required. As well as providing a reasoning approach which is more compositional, the result is the identification of the core property required of a component, thus enabling a deeper understanding about the reasons why the algorithm works correctly. This helps to reveal the reasons why the rely/guarantee approach does not work directly for some problems.
tldr: This paper proposes a more compositional verification approach for the Ben-Ari concurrent garbage collector, working around the failure of direct rely/guarantee reasoning under strong interference.
motivation: Rely/guarantee is a standard compositional verification technique for concurrent programs, but for algorithms with intense inter-component interference such as Ben-Ari's garbage collector, suitable rely and guarantee conditions cannot be constructed.
method: The author reasons that a given property holds for all instances of a particular variable, then instantiates that variable to the required local variable, enabling compositional reasoning where it would otherwise be impossible.
result: The approach verifies the Ben-Ari algorithm in a more compositional manner and identifies the core property required of a component, revealing why direct rely/guarantee reasoning fails for such problems.
conclusion: The work provides deeper insight into the limits of rely/guarantee verification and offers an alternative reasoning strategy for strongly interfering concurrent algorithms.

title: A Bulletproof Business? Towards Detecting Infrastructure-as-a-Service Offerings On Telegram
authors: Roy Ricaldi, Kristiyan Kyurkchiev, Irdin Pekaric
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cybercriminal operations increasingly depend on reusable digital infrastructure---including hosting, proxies, and virtual private networks (VPNs)---rented through Cybercrime-as-a-Service markets and advertised on platforms such as Telegram. We present a taxonomy for identifying Telegram messages advertising cybercriminal Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS). The taxonomy comprises six service categories across compute, network, and communication infrastructure, together with three trust attributes: Bulletproof, Payment Security, and Transparency. Using 261 human-annotated messages, we evaluate keyword-based and TF--IDF classifiers and examine prompt-based large language models as exploratory baselines. We select a TF--IDF pipeline and apply it to 1,116,071 messages from 167 cybercrime-related Telegram communities. The pipeline assigns at least one infrastructure category to 207,244 messages (18.57%) spanning 113 communities. Classified advertising is highly concentrated: a single community accounts for 50.3% of infrastructure-positive messages, while the trust-attribute classifiers identify Bulletproof claims in 37.66% of those messages. These findings characterize the scale, composition, and concentration of infrastructure advertising on Telegram and can inform the prioritization of communities and actors for monitoring and investigation.
tldr: The paper builds a taxonomy and TF-IDF classification pipeline to detect advertisements for cybercriminal Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) on Telegram, applying it to over a million messages from 167 communities.
motivation: Cybercriminal operations increasingly rely on rented, reusable infrastructure — hosting, proxies, VPNs — traded through Cybercrime-as-a-Service markets and advertised in Telegram communities, creating a need for automated detection at scale.
method: The authors construct a six-category IaaS taxonomy with three trust attributes (Bulletproof, Payment Security, Transparency), annotate 261 messages by hand, compare keyword-based, TF-IDF, and prompt-based LLM classifiers, and deploy the selected TF-IDF pipeline on 1,116,071 messages from 167 Telegram communities.
result: The pipeline tags 207,244 messages (18.57%) across 113 communities with at least one infrastructure category; advertising is heavily concentrated, with one community accounting for 50.3% of positive messages and Bulletproof claims appearing in 37.66% of them.
conclusion: The findings quantify the scale, composition, and concentration of illicit infrastructure advertising on Telegram, offering a basis for prioritizing communities and actors for monitoring and investigation.

title: Issuer-Sovereign Agentic Payments
authors: Dishant Sharma, Rajneesh Kaushal, Ashu Kanaujia
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are beginning to make real payments. Current approaches let an agent pay by relying on a credential provider that, in the approaches deployed today, typically sits outside the cardholder's bank. The spending rules are then enforced by the card network or that provider, and not by the bank itself. This leaves the issuing bank, which carries the financial risk, with little direct control at the moment a payment happens. This paper describes Issuer-Sovereign Agentic Payments, a method that keeps that control with the issuer. The cardholder approves a spending rule once, and the bank's own authentication component records it. Later, when the agent pays a specific merchant, the bank checks the merchant against the approved rule and generates the card authentication value only if the merchant is allowed. The payment then travels the normal card rails and is validated by the issuer, with no extra dependency introduced at execution.
tldr: The paper proposes an issuer-sovereign architecture for AI agent payments in which the cardholder's bank, rather than an external credential provider or the card network, enforces spending rules and generates card authentication values at execution time.
motivation: As AI agents begin initiating real payments, existing schemes delegate rule enforcement to credential providers or card networks that sit outside the cardholder's bank, leaving the issuer—which bears the financial risk—with little direct control over individual transactions.
method: The cardholder pre-approves a spending rule that is recorded by the bank's own authentication component; when an agent attempts payment at a specific merchant, the bank verifies the merchant against the approved rule and only then generates the card authentication value, after which the transaction proceeds over standard card rails.
result: The scheme keeps spending-rule enforcement and authentication value generation within the issuing bank, requiring no additional dependencies at payment execution while still validating through the normal card network infrastructure.
conclusion: Issuer-sovereign agentic payments offer a way to preserve issuer control over agent-initiated card transactions, but the work is a fintech/payments-security design with no connection to quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Layer-wise Discrete Certificates In Multicomponent Reacting-flow Discretizations
authors: Jingchao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multicomponent reacting-flow discretizations must conserve total species mass, preserve positive mass fractions, and dissipate a convex mixing potential. These properties are controlled at different stages of a solver, however, and a certificate established at one stage need not survive the next. We study this compatibility problem for mixture-averaged diffusion, non-orthogonal finite-volume reconstruction, and positivity-preserving Patankar time integration. The analysis is isothermal, uses prescribed density, and uses synthetic detailed-balance reaction networks for the chemistry tests. At the face level, the entropy-variable jump is shown to equal a log-mean Gibbs Hessian applied exactly to the mass-fraction jump. Requiring conservation and entropy neutrality of the mass-correction term on the simplex tangent space then yields a unique componentwise-positive face composition and an exact two-point entropy certificate. The arithmetic-weight face criterion is also satisfied by production neutral-air/carbon data and a quasi-neutral ambipolar-air control, but a face-level certificate does not automatically extend to subsequent discretization layers. A weighted least-squares non-orthogonal correction can, in the tested prototype, convert a dissipative two-point operator into an anti-dissipative multipoint operator. Likewise, Patankar rescaling can preserve positivity and conservation while increasing the free energy; an explicit finite-step rational counterexample establishes this failure independently of ensemble statistics. A fully discrete two-cell example further shows that a positive face entropy margin does not guarantee positivity of the fully discrete update. Thus conservation, positivity, and free-energy dissipation are layer-specific properties and require distinct discrete certificates.
tldr: This paper studies compatibility of discrete certificates for conservation, positivity, and entropy dissipation in multicomponent reacting-flow discretizations, showing these properties are layer-specific and do not automatically extend across solver stages.
motivation: Multicomponent reacting-flow solvers must simultaneously enforce mass conservation, positive mass fractions, and free-energy dissipation, but certificates established at one discretization stage may fail at later stages.
method: The analysis focuses on mixture-averaged diffusion, non-orthogonal finite-volume reconstruction, and positivity-preserving Patankar time integration, using isothermal assumptions, prescribed density, and synthetic detailed-balance reaction networks to derive face-level entropy certificates and test their propagation.
result: A unique componentwise-positive face composition and exact two-point entropy certificate are derived, but weighted least-squares non-orthogonal correction can make a dissipative operator anti-dissipative, and Patankar rescaling can increase free energy while preserving positivity and conservation.
conclusion: Conservation, positivity, and free-energy dissipation are layer-specific properties in reacting-flow discretizations and require distinct discrete certificates rather than being assumed to survive across stages.

title: High-Probability Sampled-Data Stabilization Of General Nonlinear Stochastic Systems
authors: Kele Sun, Yudong Wang, Shijie Zhou, Wei Lin, Xuerong Mao
abstract:
ArXiv:2609.27345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study sampled-data stabilization of general nonlinear stochastic systems under a local exponential-type Lyapunov condition for the continuous-time closed-loop system. The coefficients are assumed only locally Lipschitz, with neither linear-growth nor Khasminskii-type conditions. Two counterexamples show that almost-sure stabilization is generally unattainable. Instead, given an initial state, we establish exponential stability with arbitrarily high probability under sufficiently fast sampling. Separate methods are developed for \(p\ge 2\) and \(0

<2\), where \(p\) is the growth order in the Lyapunov condition. Numerical examples illustrate the results.
tldr: The paper studies sampled-data stabilization of general nonlinear stochastic systems under local exponential-type Lyapunov conditions, showing high-probability exponential stability with sufficiently fast sampling.
motivation: Almost-sure stabilization is generally unattainable for such systems, as demonstrated by two counterexamples, motivating a weaker high-probability stabilization framework.
method: The authors develop separate analyses for growth orders p >= 2 and 0 < p < 2, using local exponential Lyapunov conditions, locally Lipschitz coefficients, and sufficiently fast sampling.
result: Given an initial state, exponential stability is established with arbitrarily high probability under fast enough sampling, and numerical examples illustrate the theoretical findings.
conclusion: The work provides a probabilistic stabilization theory for nonlinear stochastic systems without linear-growth or Khasminskii-type conditions, extending sampled-data control to a broader class of systems.

title: Divide And Doubt: Diverse Distributed Poisoning For Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Tianhao Chen, Yuhan Wei, Weifei Jin, Zhengyuan Jiang, Yuepeng Hu, Neil Zhenqiang Gong
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-passage corpus poisoning often repeats one target claim across similar documents, creating correlated lexical and semantic patterns that similarity- and conflict-aware defenses can suppress jointly. We introduce DnD (Divide and Doubt), a targeted attack based on two principles: distributing support for the target answer across stylistically diverse passages, and including a passage that casts doubt on evidence for the reference answer. The first disperses poison-passage representations in embedding space, while the second strengthens target adoption when multiple poisoned passages are retrieved. We evaluate DnD on two open-domain QA datasets across three LLMs and nine RAG configurations, under both black-box and white-box access to the retriever. Across these settings, DnD matches or outperforms prior attacks in most configurations, with its largest gains against clustering- and conflict-aware defenses.
tldr: DnD is a distributed poisoning attack that spreads malicious support across stylistically diverse passages and includes a doubt-casting passage to improve target adoption in retrieval-augmented generation.
motivation: Existing multi-passage corpus poisoning attacks often repeat one target claim, creating detectable lexical and semantic patterns that similarity- and conflict-aware defenses can suppress.
method: The attack distributes support for the target answer across stylistically diverse passages to disperse poison representations in embedding space, and adds a passage that casts doubt on evidence for the reference answer.
result: DnD matches or outperforms prior attacks across two open-domain QA datasets, three LLMs, and nine RAG configurations under black-box and white-box retriever access, with largest gains against clustering- and conflict-aware defenses.
conclusion: The paper demonstrates that diversifying poison passages and injecting doubt can substantially strengthen corpus poisoning attacks against retrieval-augmented generation defenses.

title: Solidity Meets LLMs: A Transformer-Based Approach To Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection
authors: Djamel Eddine Hakim Ghorab, Farid Mokhati, Mostafa Anouar Ghorab
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing adoption of blockchain technologies, particularly the Ethereum platform, has amplified the critical role of smart contracts in decentralized applications. However, the increasing complexity and financial value of these contracts make them prime targets for cyber attacks. In this work, we present a transformer-based approach for the detection of vulnerabilities in smart contract fragments written in Solidity. Leveraging the representational power of pre-trained Large Language Models (LLMs), we construct a robust pipeline that includes the definition of a ground truth dataset, labeling code fragments as vulnerable or safe. We then fine-tune a BERT-based architecture on this dataset, enabling the model to capture the syntactic and semantic patterns specific to Solidity code. Our fine-tuned model demonstrates strong performance, achieving an F1 score of 92%, and highlighting the effectiveness of LLM adaptation in enhancing smart contract security through deep contextual understanding.
tldr: A transformer-based (BERT) fine-tuned model detects vulnerabilities in Solidity smart contract fragments, achieving 92% F1.
motivation: Smart contracts on Ethereum hold increasing financial value and complexity, making them attractive targets for cyber attacks, so automated vulnerability detection is needed.
method: The authors build a labeled ground-truth dataset of vulnerable and safe Solidity code fragments and fine-tune a pre-trained BERT-based LLM to capture Solidity-specific syntactic and semantic patterns.
result: The fine-tuned BERT model reaches an F1 score of 92%, demonstrating that LLM adaptation provides effective deep contextual understanding for smart contract security.
conclusion: LLM adaptation is a promising route for smart contract vulnerability detection, though the work is entirely within blockchain security and software engineering.

title: The Power Of Recruiting The Smaller Side: Two Additional Traders Suffice In Two-Sided Markets
authors: Yang Cai, Vineet Gupta, Yanchen Jiang, Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Grigoris Velegkas, Di Wang, Mingfei Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Bulow-Klemperer-style competition complexity in two-sided double auctions with [MATH] unit-demand buyers drawn i.i.d. from [MATH] and [MATH] unit-supply sellers drawn i.i.d. from [MATH]. When [MATH] and buyer valuations first-order stochastically dominate seller costs ([MATH]), we prove that recruiting just two additional sellers enables Seller Trade Reduction (STR), a prior-independent mechanism, to achieve expected Gains From Trade (GFT) at least the first-best GFT of the original market. When the buyer side is the smaller side of the market ([MATH]), an analogous result holds for Buyer Trade Reduction with 2 additional buyers. This resolves open questions of Babaioff, Goldner, and Gonczarowski (SODA 2020) and Cai, Liaw, Mehta, and Zhao (STOC 2024). We complement our upper bound by showing that this uniform bound is optimal: already for [MATH], no prior-free mechanism (deterministic or randomized) that is dominant-strategy incentive-compatible, individually rational, and weakly budget-balanced can match the first-best GFT by recruiting only one additional seller.
tldr: The paper studies competition complexity in two-sided double auctions and proves that recruiting just two additional sellers or buyers suffices for trade-reduction mechanisms to match first-best gains from trade under stochastic dominance conditions.
motivation: Prior work left open the exact number of additional participants needed in two-sided markets for prior-independent mechanisms to achieve first-best gains from trade, motivating sharp bounds on competition complexity.
method: The authors analyze Bulow-Klemperer-style competition complexity for double auctions, proving upper bounds for Seller Trade Reduction and Buyer Trade Reduction with two extra agents and a matching lower bound for prior-free dominant-strategy incentive-compatible mechanisms.
result: They show that two additional sellers (or buyers when that side is smaller) enable STR (or BTR) to recover the original market's first-best GFT, and that one additional seller is insufficient for any prior-free, weakly budget-balanced, dominant-strategy incentive-compatible mechanism.
conclusion: The work resolves open questions in the competition complexity of two-sided markets and establishes the optimality of the uniform two-agent bound for trade-reduction mechanisms.

title: JEV-Star: Fast, Low-Cost StarCraft Ii Control With Language-Model Planning
authors: Weiyu Ma, Liangbing Zhao, Yongcheng Zeng, Jian Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present JEV-Star, a StarCraft II controller that defeats the strongest non-cheating built-in AI, Lv7, by combining fast JEV action selection with persistent GPT-6 planning. The combined system wins four full games at Lv5--Lv7, including two Lv7 victories with different seeds, while retaining a median JEV response time of 0.422 seconds. Mean estimated model cost across these games is USD~3.71 per game: USD~0.15 for JEV and USD~3.56 for GPT-6. We compare this system with an initial JEV-only controller in full-game macro control and multi-unit micromanagement. The standalone controller reaches a 20-minute limit against Lv2 without expanding. Across 35 battle maps with three episodes per map and controller, the combined system raises mean enemy elimination from 16.50\% to 37.69\% and wins from 3 to 7 out of 105. Replay frames and decision logs document resource reservation, persistent economic goals, and stable army objectives in successful full games. The results demonstrate a practical division between inexpensive, subsecond decisions and longer-horizon planning. The comparison evaluates complete systems; concurrent interface improvements mean that planning's contribution is not isolated by a controlled ablation. Code is available at [URL].
tldr: JEV-Star combines fast JEV action selection with persistent GPT-6 planning to control StarCraft II, achieving Lv7 victories at modest latency and cost.
motivation: Real-time strategy games like StarCraft II require both fast reactive decisions and long-horizon strategic planning, a tension that motivates hybridizing cheap low-level controllers with expensive language-model planners.
method: The authors pair a JEV-based action selector (subsecond responses) with a persistent GPT-6 planning module that maintains economic and army objectives, evaluated on full games and 35 battle maps against built-in AIs.
result: The combined system wins four full games at Lv5–Lv7 (two at Lv7 with different seeds) with median JEV response time of 0.422 s and mean cost of about USD 3.71 per game, raising mean enemy elimination from 16.50% to 37.69% and battle-map wins from 3 to 7 out of 105.
conclusion: The results support a practical division of labor between inexpensive subsecond decisions and longer-horizon LLM planning, though concurrent interface changes prevent isolating planning's contribution via ablation.

title: Ramp: Reversing Adversarial Perturbations To Strengthen Clean-Label Backdoor Attacks Against Malware Detectors
authors: Jinwen Xin, Dongni Zhang, Chenyang Wang, Jianming Fu, Ming Tang, Guojun Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning-based malware detectors are commonly updated by fine-tuning on newly collected samples, but this practical update pipeline also creates an attack surface for training-time backdoor attacks. In realistic crowdsourced data collection, however, strict label vetting typically restricts attackers to the clean-label setting, in which poisoned samples must retain benign labels and functionality, making effective backdoor injection substantially harder. We present a new attack perspective based on feature-space manipulation: instead of relying solely on stronger trigger designs or selecting benign samples that are naturally similar to malware, we deliberately construct benign programs whose representations shift toward the malware region before trigger injection, thereby creating stronger feature-label conflicts during training. Based on this insight, we propose RAMP, an attack enhancement method that uses a genetic algorithm to optimize reversed adversarial perturbations under black-box access and then injects them through functionality-preserving binary manipulations. Extensive experiments show that RAMP substantially improves attack effectiveness over trigger-only baselines, with especially pronounced gains at low poisoning ratios, while maintaining accuracy on clean data. Moreover, RAMP can be combined with advanced trigger designs.
tldr: RAMP enhances clean-label backdoor attacks against malware detectors by reversing adversarial perturbations to shift benign program representations toward the malware region before trigger injection.
motivation: Deep learning-based malware detectors are vulnerable to training-time backdoor attacks, but strict label vetting in crowdsourced data collection forces attackers into the clean-label setting where effective poisoning is difficult.
method: RAMP uses a genetic algorithm under black-box access to optimize reversed adversarial perturbations and injects them via functionality-preserving binary manipulations, creating stronger feature-label conflicts during training.
result: Extensive experiments show RAMP substantially improves attack effectiveness over trigger-only baselines, especially at low poisoning ratios, while maintaining clean-data accuracy and combining well with advanced trigger designs.
conclusion: Feature-space manipulation through reversed adversarial perturbations offers a practical and effective enhancement for clean-label backdoor attacks on malware detectors.

title: Evage: Autonomous Mev Generation And Adaptation Via Multi-Agent Harness
authors: Yan Wen, Zichun Cai, Iliya Mirzaei, Xiaohua Cai, Mohammad Javad Amiri, Haoxian Chen, Chenyuan Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) has evolved into a major economic force in blockchain ecosystems, yet its capture is dominated by experienced teams, and both strategy design and implementation rely on manual expert work that scales poorly across heterogeneous protocols and chains. We present EVAGE, the first fully autonomous multi-agent framework for end-to-end MEV strategy generation and adaptation. Equipped with three specialized operation modes, it automatically discovers novel MEV variants, adapts execution logic across disparate protocols, and ports strategies between chains, including Layer-1 and Layer-2 networks. To avoid inference latency on the critical MEV execution path, EVAGE generates and refines MEV bot code offline rather than making real-time decisions directly. Under the coordination of an orchestrator agent, three specialized subagents collectively implement and repair the full MEV bot workflow via closed-loop diagnostics, eliminating human intervention while producing validated and deterministic Proof-of-Concept implementations. We evaluate EVAGE on over 1.5M blocks from each of Ethereum, Base, and BNB Smart Chain (BSC). On Ethereum, EVAGE uncovers five novel MEV strategy variants, yielding a profit increase of 1.02[MATH] to 15.97[MATH]. It also successfully adapts 11 MEV strategies from CPMM to both CLMM and Balancer V2 and ports strategies from Ethereum to Base and BSC, all with less than 60 dollars in LLM token costs.
tldr: EVAGE is a fully autonomous multi-agent LLM framework that generates, adapts, and ports MEV (Maximal Extractable Value) strategies across blockchain protocols and chains.
motivation: MEV capture in blockchain ecosystems is dominated by expert teams because strategy design and implementation remain manual, which scales poorly across heterogeneous protocols and chains.
method: Three specialized subagents under an orchestrator agent implement and repair MEV bot workflows via closed-loop diagnostics, generating and refining bot code offline to avoid inference latency on the execution path.
result: Evaluated on over 1.5M blocks each from Ethereum, Base, and BSC, EVAGE uncovered five novel MEV strategy variants on Ethereum with profit increases up to 15.97x, adapted 11 strategies from CPMM to CLMM and Balancer V2, and ported strategies across chains for under $60 in LLM token costs.
conclusion: Autonomous multi-agent code generation can automate end-to-end MEV strategy discovery and adaptation, removing the need for human expert intervention in blockchain value extraction.

title: Agentic Ai Cybersecurity Framework
authors: Victor Kebande
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing scale, complexity, and dynamism of modern cyber threats have rendered traditional reactive cybersecurity mechanisms insufficient. This paper introduces an Agentic AI Cybersecurity Framework (AACF) designed to enable autonomous, goal-driven, and adaptive cyber defense operations. Unlike conventional systems that rely on predefined rules and human intervention, the proposed framework leverages agentic artificial intelligence to perceive environmental states, reason about potential threats, and execute context-aware responses with minimal supervision. The framework is structured into key functional layers, including perception, reasoning, decisionmaking, action execution, and feedback-driven learning, enabling continuous adaptation to evolving attack patterns. By integrating intelligent agents with real-time data analysis and automated response mechanisms, AACF supports proactive threat detection, dynamic risk assessment, and coordinated mitigation strategies across distributed environments. A conceptual architecture is presented, along with illustrative use cases demonstrating its applicability to intrusion detection, incident response, and autonomous security orchestration. The proposed framework contributes to the emerging paradigm of self-directed cybersecurity systems and provides a foundation for developing resilient, scalable, and intelligent defense infrastructures.
tldr: The paper introduces an Agentic AI Cybersecurity Framework (AACF) for autonomous, adaptive cyber defense using agentic AI with perception, reasoning, decision-making, action, and feedback layers.
motivation: Traditional reactive cybersecurity mechanisms are insufficient for modern threats due to increasing scale, complexity, and dynamism.
method: A conceptual layered architecture is proposed that integrates intelligent agents with real-time data analysis and automated response mechanisms to enable proactive threat detection and mitigation.
result: The framework is illustrated with use cases for intrusion detection, incident response, and autonomous security orchestration, demonstrating its applicability to distributed environments.
conclusion: AACF contributes to the emerging paradigm of self-directed cybersecurity systems and provides a foundation for resilient, scalable, and intelligent defense infrastructures.

title: Quantum Chemistry In A Novel Hybrid Dipolar Atom-Ion Mixture
authors: Claudia Galantini, Mateo Londo\~no, Luc Verwaal, Edgar J. D. Vredenbregt, Jes\'us P\'erez-R\'ios, Rianne S. Lous
abstract: ArXiv:2609.26859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Merging trapped ions with cold atomic clouds offers intriguing prospects for quantum chemistry and many-body quantum simulations. Especially when going beyond the standard alkali atomic baths by using lanthanide atoms, opportunities arise to study the interplay between the intermediate-range atom-ion interaction and the tunable long-range dipolar atom-atom interactions. However, the high total angular momentum of the ground-state of open-shell lanthanides, e.g. [MATH] for dysprosium, affects the atom-ion potential. Here, we discuss the implications for long- and short-range atom-ion interactions and present a novel apparatus which combines an ytterbium ion (Yb[MATH]) with dipolar dysprosium (Dy) atoms. We highlight the consequences of this novel Dy-Yb[MATH] mixture for observing buffer gas cooling, (non-) radiative charge transfer, and three-body recombination. While the energy-averaged rates are dominated by radiative charge transfer, particularly radiative association, we find that three-body recombination can compete with molecular-ion formation at Dy densities [MATH] cm[MATH]. This competition is further enhanced by the expected non-thermal distribution of ion energies. These processes could be experimentally characterised through controlled variation of the atom-ion interaction parameters, providing a direct test of our theoretical predictions.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Foliations And Minimality For Twist Maps
authors: Julian Lazaro Aguirre Salvador Addas Zanata
abstract: ArXiv:2609.27102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we consider area-preserving twist maps [MATH] with vertical rotation sets reduced to a single irrational number [MATH]. Our first result states that under these hypotheses, there exists a [MATH]-invariant foliation [MATH], where each function [MATH] is [MATH]-Lipschitz for some constant [MATH]. Moreover, we also prove that in case [MATH] is a Lipschitz foliation and the leaf dynamics, which is always a transitive circle homeomorphism of rotation number [MATH], is bi-Lipschitz conjugate to the irrational rotation [MATH], then [MATH] is minimal.
tldr: This paper studies area-preserving twist maps with a single irrational vertical rotation number, proving existence of a Lipschitz invariant foliation and conditions under which the map is minimal.
motivation: The work addresses structural properties of twist maps in dynamical systems, specifically the existence and regularity of invariant foliations and minimality when leaf dynamics are bi-Lipschitz conjugate to irrational rotations.
method: The authors use techniques from dynamical systems and topological dynamics, analyzing vertical rotation sets and constructing invariant foliations under Lipschitz conditions.
result: Under the given hypotheses, an invariant foliation exists with Lipschitz leaf functions; if the foliation is Lipschitz and leaf dynamics are bi-Lipschitz conjugate to an irrational rotation, the map is minimal.
conclusion: The paper establishes new results on the existence of invariant foliations and minimality criteria for area-preserving twist maps, contributing to the theory of dynamical systems but unrelated to quantum information science.
